title: From Simulators to Digital Twins for Enabling Emerging Cellular Networks: A Tutorial and Survey
authors: Marvin Manalastas; Muhammad Umar Bin Farooq; Syed Muhammad Asad Zaidi; Haneya Naeem Qureshi; Yusuf Sambo; Ali Imran
summary: Tutorial and survey that reviews 5G-and-beyond simulators as digital system models and evaluates them for use as building blocks of cellular digital twins.
method: Tutorial, taxonomy and metric-based comparison of simulators
key_result: Introduces realism, completeness and computational-efficiency metrics and an applicability matrix mapping simulators to research themes.
limitation_or_critique: Centred on RAN/system-level simulators; core-network emulators (Open5GS, free5GC) and control-plane twinning receive comparatively little attention.

title: A comprehensive survey of Network Digital Twin architecture, capabilities, challenges, and requirements for Edge–Cloud Continuum
authors: Syed Mohsan Raza; Roberto Minerva; Noel Crespi; Maira Alvi; Manoj Herath; Hrishikesh Dutta
summary: Surveys NDT specifications, components and AI/ML integration and examines their gaps when the twinned system is an edge-cloud continuum with stakeholders beyond the network operator.
method: Literature and specification survey plus proposed NDT data model
key_result: Argues current NDT specifications serve operators only and proposes a data model with descriptive and prescriptive features for other stakeholders.
limitation_or_critique: Focus on edge-cloud continuum rather than the 3GPP 5G core; proposed data model is not validated against TS 28.561 information models.
standards_link: ITU-T Y.3090; IRTF NMRG NDT draft

title: Network Digital Twin: Context, Enabling Technologies, and Opportunities
authors: Paul Almasan; Miquel Ferriol-Galmes; Jordi Paillisse; Jose Suarez-Varela; Diego Perino; Diego Lopez; Antonio Agustin Pastor Perales; Paul Harvey; Laurent Ciavaglia; Leon Wong; Vishnu Ram; Shihan Xiao; Xiang Shi; Xiangle Cheng; Albert Cabellos-Aparicio; Pere Barlet-Ros
summary: Positions the network digital twin as a renewed form of network modelling built from data-driven ML models that run in real time, outlines its general architecture and illustrates it with an ML-based performance model used for QoS-aware routing optimisation.
method: Tutorial/position article with ML (GNN-based) network model case study
key_result: Shows that an ML-based NDT can replace slow simulators inside an optimisation loop to evaluate candidate routing configurations.
limitation_or_critique: Case study targets IP/transport routing rather than the 5G core control plane, and the OpenAlex citation count looks anomalously low for this widely referenced article.

title: Digital-Twin-Enabled 6G: Vision, Architectural Trends, and Future Directions
authors: Latif U. Khan; Walid Saad; Dusit Niyato; Zhu Han; Choong Seon Hong
summary: Vision article arguing that digital twins can serve as the management, operation and optimisation framework of 6G, covering design requirements and edge-, cloud- and edge-cloud-based twin architectures.
method: Vision/overview with comparative taxonomy of twin placements
key_result: Highly cited reference architecture distinguishing edge, cloud and hybrid twin deployments and listing research directions for 6G twins.
limitation_or_critique: Conceptual and IoE/application-oriented; it offers no evaluation and no mapping to 3GPP core network functions or management services.

title: Empowering 6G Communication Systems With Digital Twin Technology: A Comprehensive Survey
authors: Nandish P. Kuruvatti; Mohammad Asif Habibi; Sanket Partani; Bin Han; Amina Fellan; Hans D. Schotten
summary: Survey on how digital twins can support research, development, operation and optimisation of 6G communication systems, discussed from the viewpoint of operators, vendors and standardisation bodies.
method: Literature survey
key_result: Maps DT use across the 6G system lifecycle and links it to stakeholder and SDO requirements.
limitation_or_critique: Pre-dates the 3GPP SA5 NDT study (TR 28.915) and therefore cannot reflect the standardised NDT management model; little quantitative evidence.

title: Digital Twins: A Survey on Enabling Technologies, Challenges, Trends and Future Prospects
authors: Stefan Mihai; Mahnoor Yaqoob; Dang V. Hung; William Davis; Praveer Towakel; Mohsin Raza; Mehmet Karamanoglu; Balbir Barn; Dattaprasad Shetve; Raja V. Prasad; Hrishikesh Venkataraman; Ramona Trestian; Huan X. Nguyen
summary: Large COMST survey of digital twin enabling technologies (IoT, AI, 5G/6G, AR/VR, distributed computing) and of challenges such as data availability, fidelity and missing validation methods across industries.
method: Literature survey
key_result: Identifies the lack of standard development methodologies and validation measures as a cross-domain obstacle for digital twins.
limitation_or_critique: Generic, industry-wide view in which communication networks are mostly an enabler of twins rather than the twinned system, so it gives limited guidance for core-network NDTs.

title: Digital Twin Networks: A Survey
authors: Yiwen Wu; Ke Zhang; Yan Zhang
summary: Broad survey that defines digital twin networks (DTN), reviews their modelling, communication, computing and data-processing enablers, and lists application domains of which 6G is only one.
method: Literature survey
key_result: Provides an early, widely cited definition and taxonomy of DTN features, key technologies and open issues.
limitation_or_critique: Cross-domain scope (manufacturing, aviation, healthcare, cities) means mobile-core twinning, 3GPP management and validation of network changes are barely treated.

title: Towards Network Data Analytics in 5G Systems and Beyond
authors: Marcos Lima Romero; Ricardo Suyama
venue: Anais do XLIII Simpósio Brasileiro de Telecomunicações e Processamento de Sinais
summary: Reviews more than 70 NWDAF research articles to map methods and use cases and proposes two new NWDAF use cases oriented to operator monetisation.
method: literature review + use-case proposal
key_result: Finds that academic NWDAF work concentrates on a narrow set of methods and use cases, largely dictated by which datasets are available.
limitation_or_critique: Regional symposium paper (also on arXiv 2506.04860) with a short-format review; selection method and depth are limited compared with a journal survey.

title: Network Automation and Data Analytics in 3GPP 5G Systems
authors: Miguel-Angel Garcia-Martin; Marco Gramaglia; Pablo Serrano
summary: Tutorial-style overview of the 3GPP network automation ecosystem built around NWDAF, covering its functionality, consumers and use cases from Release 15/16 and the extensions of Releases 17 and 18.
method: standards review / tutorial
key_result: Shows how NWDAF evolved from a single slice-load use case into a general analytics producer feeding automated NF decisions across many use cases.
limitation_or_critique: Descriptive standards overview with no quantitative evaluation and no systematic coverage of the academic ML literature or of Rel-19 AI/ML enhancements.

title: A Survey of 3GPP Release 18 on Network Data Analytics Function Management
authors: Yuxia Niu; Song Zhao; Xiaoming She; Peng Chen
venue: 2022 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
summary: Surveys the Release 18 key issues and candidate solutions for managing NWDAF itself, including NRM support for multiple NWDAFs, logical decomposition and NWDAF performance management.
method: standards survey (SA5 study items)
key_result: Identifies NRM modelling of decomposed/multiple NWDAF instances and performance management of data collection and analytics output as open management issues.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper restating 3GPP study-item content, without evaluation and with limited link to ML lifecycle research.

title: Reliability and Availability in Virtualized Networks: A Survey on Standards, Modeling Approaches, and Research Challenges
authors: Mario Di Mauro; Walter Cerroni; Fabio Postiglione; Massimo Tornatore; Kishor S. Trivedi
summary: Survey of reliability and availability of NFV-based networks from a modelling viewpoint, covering ETSI NFV-REL standardisation, formalisms for failure/repair behaviour, tools and open challenges.
method: survey of availability/reliability modelling (RBD, Markov chains, SRN/SPN, etc.)
key_result: Provides a structured map from ETSI NFV reliability requirements to stochastic modelling formalisms and lists open research challenges for fault-tolerant virtualised systems.
limitation_or_critique: Centred on generic NFV rather than 5GC service-based procedures, and it does not address 3GPP restoration (TS 23.527), NF sets or ML-driven failure prediction in depth.

title: Fault Tolerance in Service Function Chains: A Taxonomy, Survey and Future Directions
authors: Muhammad Hamza Shahab; Yogesh Sharma
venue: Journal of Network and Systems Management
summary: Systematic review of fault tolerance for virtualised service function chains, with a taxonomy based on failure types, occurrence patterns, management approaches and evaluation metrics.
method: systematic literature review and taxonomy
key_result: Proposes a taxonomy and a conceptual framework for highly fault-tolerant SFCs, and identifies trends and research gaps in failure management.
limitation_or_critique: SFC-generic; it does not specifically treat 5GC control-plane state, 3GPP NF set/restoration procedures or geo-redundant core deployments (judged from the abstract of the preprint version).

title: Resilience-by-Design in 6G Networks: Literature Review and Novel Enabling Concepts
authors: Ladan Khaloopour; Yanpeng Su; Florian Raskob; Tobias Meuser; Roland Bless; Leon Janzen; Kamyar Abedi; Marko Andjelkovic; Hekma Chaari; Pousali Chakraborty; Michael Kreutzer; Matthias Hollick; Thorsten Strufe; Norman Franchi; Vahid Jamali
summary: Literature review of resilience definitions and approaches and a proposal of resilience-by-design principles applied across all 6G layers, from electronics to network functions and services (Open6GHub).
method: literature review and conceptual framework
key_result: Organises resilience enablers into a multi-level resilience-by-design concept and discusses how each principle maps to 6G layers including core network components.
limitation_or_critique: Broad and conceptual; core-network failover, state replication and quantitative availability targets receive only limited, non-evaluated treatment.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Communication Networks: Context, Use Cases and Opportunities
authors: José Suárez-Varela; Paul Almasan; Miquel Ferriol-Galmés; Krzysztof Rusek; Fabien Geyer; Xiangle Cheng; Xiang Shi; Shihan Xiao; Franco Scarselli; Albert Cabellos-Aparicio; Pere Barlet-Ros
summary: Position paper and tutorial arguing that GNNs are a core tool for modelling, controlling and managing communication networks, illustrated with one wired and one wireless state-of-the-art GNN model.
method: GNN tutorial and position paper
data_or_testbed: n/a (illustrative wired and wireless case studies)
key_result: Identifies generalisation to unseen topologies and configurations as the main advantage of GNNs over conventional neural networks for networking.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-length overview centred on the authors' own models, with no coverage of mobile core functions or 3GPP analytics frameworks.

title: Digital Twin for Networking: A Data-Driven Performance Modeling Perspective
authors: Linbo Hui; Mowei Wang; Liang Zhang; Lu Lu; Yong Cui
summary: Survey of data-driven performance models as the engine of network digital twins, framed by fidelity, efficiency and flexibility requirements for what-if evaluation.
method: Survey and comparison of data-driven performance models
key_result: Finds a persistent tension between the input diversity performance models must handle and the limited data obtainable from production networks.
limitation_or_critique: Concentrates on wired/data-center performance models and offers no mapping to mobile core functions or to standardised digital twin frameworks.

title: Graph-based deep learning for communication networks: A survey
authors: Weiwei Jiang
summary: Survey of graph convolutional, graph attention and related graph-based deep learning methods applied to wired, wireless and SDN problems, organised by problem and proposed solution.
method: Literature survey
key_result: Claims to be the first survey to cover graph-based deep learning for both wired and wireless networks and catalogues problems such as traffic prediction, routing and resource allocation.
limitation_or_critique: Broad catalogue that stops in 2021 and does not discuss service-based 5G core functions, digital twins or operational deployment.

title: Cellular traffic prediction with machine learning: A survey
authors: Weiwei Jiang
summary: Survey of machine-learning and deep-learning approaches to cellular traffic prediction, classifying prediction problems, model families and evaluation metrics.
method: Literature survey
key_result: Provides a taxonomy of cellular traffic prediction problems, models and metrics and lists open research directions.
limitation_or_critique: Focused on RAN/cell-level traffic volumes rather than control-plane or core network function load, and predates transformer and foundation-model work.

title: LLM-Powered Agentic AI for 5G/6G Networks: A Tutorial and Survey on Architectures, Protocols, and Standardization
authors: Mazene Ameur; Abdelkader Mekrache; Bouziane Brik; Adlen Ksentini
summary: Two-part tutorial-survey that formalises control, management and AI-native planes of 5G/6G and maps agentic capabilities (reasoning, planning, tool use, multi-agent coordination) onto them.
method: Tutorial and survey with standardisation mapping
key_result: Argues that prior surveys treat agentic AI and mobile networks separately and links agent capabilities to concrete 5G/6G control surfaces and 6G initiatives.
limitation_or_critique: Under-review preprint not yet peer reviewed; as a tutorial it gives no new experimental evidence on agent reliability in core networks.

title: Zero Touch Management: A Survey of Network Automation Solutions for 5G and 6G Networks
authors: Estefania Coronado; Rasoul Behravesh; Tejas Subramanya; Adriana Fernandez-Fernandez; Muhammad Shuaib Siddiqui; Xavier Costa-Perez; Roberto Riggio
summary: Surveys zero-touch management for mobile networks, defining it as fully autonomous management under human oversight and reviewing automation solutions from RAN to core.
method: Survey with taxonomy of network management approaches and enablers
key_result: Provides a taxonomy linking autonomous-network concepts, ZSM-related standardisation and enabling technologies (AI/ML, digital twins, intent) across RAN, transport and core.
limitation_or_critique: Written before the LLM/agentic wave and before 3GPP Rel-18 intent and autonomy-level work matured, so it does not cover generative-AI loops or Rel-18+ management services.
standards_link: ETSI GS ZSM 002; ETSI ZSM 009; 3GPP SA5 management

title: Large Language Model (LLM) for Telecommunications: A Comprehensive Survey on Principles, Key Techniques, and Opportunities
authors: Hao Zhou; Chengming Hu; Ye Yuan; Yufei Cui; Yili Jin; Can Chen; Haolun Wu; Dun Yuan; Li Jiang; Di Wu; Xue Liu; Jianzhong Zhang; Xianbin Wang; Jiangchuan Liu
summary: Comprehensive survey of LLM fundamentals and their telecom uses grouped into generation, classification, optimisation and prediction tasks, including network configuration generation.
method: Survey of LLM techniques mapped to telecom problem classes
key_result: Catalogues LLM-enabled configuration generation, RL reward design and time-series prediction as building blocks for automated network management.
limitation_or_critique: Broad telecom scope with physical-layer emphasis; core-network operation, closed-loop safety and alignment with 3GPP management services receive little attention.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM‐Based Network Management and Operations
authors: Jibum Hong; Nguyen Van Tu; James Won‐Ki Hong
summary: Surveys LLM-based approaches to network management and operations and contrasts them with earlier rule-based and ML-based self-driving network methods.
method: Survey and comparison with conventional approaches
key_result: Identifies intent interpretation and task automation as main strengths of LLMs and hallucination and domain adaptation as main obstacles.
limitation_or_critique: Generic network-management focus (mostly IP/enterprise); mobile core specific functions and 3GPP management interfaces are not treated in depth.

title: A Survey on Intent-Based Networking
authors: Aris Leivadeas; Matthias Falkner
summary: Detailed survey of intent-based networking organised around intent expression, translation, resolution, activation and assurance as stages of one closed loop.
method: Survey structured by intent lifecycle stages
key_result: Positions intent assurance as the feedback stage that closes the automation loop and catalogues techniques for each lifecycle stage.
limitation_or_critique: Mostly generic IP/SDN oriented with little mobile-core specificity, and it predates LLM-based intent translation that now dominates the field.

title: Intent-driven autonomous network and service management in future cellular networks: A structured literature review
authors: Kashif Mehmood; Katina Kralevska; David Palma
summary: Structured literature review of intent-based management for cellular networks covering intent models, lifecycle management and a converged architecture over NFV/SDN.
method: Structured literature review and proposed generalised IBN framework
key_result: Identifies the need for domain-agnostic intent representation models and for intents to act as first-class policies in service modelling.
limitation_or_critique: Proposed converged framework is conceptual and not validated, and coverage stops before LLM-based intent handling and 3GPP Rel-18 intent services.

title: A survey on Zero touch network and Service Management (ZSM) for 5G and beyond networks
authors: Madhusanka Liyanage; Quoc-Viet Pham; Kapal Dev; Sweta Bhattacharya; Praveen Kumar Reddy Maddikunta; Thippa Reddy Gadekallu; Gokul Yenduri
venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications
summary: Comprehensive review of the end-to-end ZSM architecture, its components and interfaces, and research on ZSM automation, cross-domain service lifecycle management and security.
method: Survey of architecture, standards and research projects
key_result: Maps ZSM building blocks to self-configuration, self-monitoring, self-healing and self-optimisation functions and summarises related SDO and project activity.
limitation_or_critique: Largely descriptive and framework-oriented; offers little quantitative comparison of closed-loop solutions and limited treatment of 3GPP 5G core analytics (NWDAF/MDA) as loop inputs.

title: A Survey of AIOps in the Era of Large Language Models
authors: Lingzhe Zhang; Tong Jia; Mengxi Jia; Yifan Wu; Aiwei Liu; Yong Yang; Zhonghai Wu; Xuming Hu; Philip Yu; Ying Li
summary: Surveys 183 papers from 2020-2024 on using large language models for AIOps, analysing data sources, task evolution, LLM-based methods and evaluation practices.
method: Systematic literature review (four research questions)
key_result: Maps how LLMs reshape failure data processing and enable new AIOps tasks such as incident summarisation and agent-based root-cause analysis.
limitation_or_critique: Focused on software/cloud operations; telecom core networks and standardised analytics functions are essentially absent from the reviewed corpus.

title: Fault Prediction for Heterogeneous Telecommunication Networks Using Machine Learning: A Survey
authors: Killian Murphy; Antoine Lavignotte; Catherine Lepers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Telecom-specific survey of machine-learning network fault prediction, framed from the viewpoint of a network and system integrator handling heterogeneous equipment.
method: Literature survey plus a cost-oriented evaluation metric
key_result: Introduces a metric measuring expected maintenance-cost reduction from a predictive model and gives recommendations for ML use in telecom fault prediction.
limitation_or_critique: Equipment-level fault prediction dominates; cloud-native 5G core functions and 3GPP NWDAF/MDAF analytics are not a central focus.

title: Anomaly Detection and Failure Root Cause Analysis in (Micro) Service-Based Cloud Applications: A Survey
authors: Jacopo Soldani; Antonio Brogi
summary: Structured qualitative survey classifying anomaly-detection and root-cause-analysis techniques for multi-service cloud applications by the observability data they consume (logs, metrics, traces).
method: Literature survey and taxonomy
key_result: Provides a taxonomy that separates detection from RCA techniques and lists open challenges for microservice-based systems.
limitation_or_critique: Covers generic cloud applications only and predates both LLM-based RCA and telecom-specific cloud-native network functions.

title: A Survey of AIOps Methods for Failure Management
authors: Paolo Notaro; Jorge Cardoso; Michael Gerndt
venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
summary: Reviews about one hundred AIOps failure-management solutions and organises them into five categories and fourteen subcategories according to their intervention time window.
method: Systematic literature review
key_result: Proposes a reference taxonomy (failure prevention, prediction, detection, root-cause analysis, remediation) widely reused in later AIOps work.
limitation_or_critique: IT-operations oriented, with no treatment of telecom network functions or of 3GPP management analytics.

title: A Survey on Cloud-Based 6G Deployments: Current Solutions, Future Directions and Open Challenges
authors: Tolga O. Atalay; Alireza Famili; Amirreza Ghafoori; Angelos Stavrou
summary: Large survey of deploying cellular (5G/6G) core and network functions on public clouds and Kubernetes, with a taxonomy over architecture, orchestration, multi-tenancy and economics.
method: Survey with four-dimension taxonomy and analysis of six investigation areas
key_result: Identifies scalability/elasticity, performance and resilience as key open areas and points to AI-driven orchestration and serverless networking as emerging trends for 6G cores.
limitation_or_critique: Unreviewed preprint; breadth over depth, so NF selection/SCP and learning-based scaling receive only summary treatment.

title: VNF and CNF Placement in 5G: Recent Advances and Future Trends
authors: Wissal Attaoui; Essaid Sabir; Halima Elbiaze; Mohsen Guizani
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Survey that builds a taxonomy of optimisation techniques for placing virtualised and containerised network functions in 5G, extending the classic VNF placement problem to CNFs in edge/fog settings.
method: Systematic survey and taxonomy (metrics, methods, algorithms, environment)
key_result: Organises VNF/CNF placement literature by objective (latency, congestion, utilisation, energy) and solution class (exact, heuristic, ML), and lists open problems for cloud-native 5G.
limitation_or_critique: Treats placement generically for VNFs/CNFs and does not specifically model 5GC control-plane semantics such as NRF/SCP-mediated NF selection.

title: Cloud-Native Service Mesh Readiness for 5G and Beyond
authors: Saidulu Aldas; Andrew Babakian
summary: Review-style analysis of how service meshes can realise the 3GPP SBA in cloud-native deployments, covering service-to-service communication, discovery and programmability for 5G core signalling.
method: Qualitative review and architectural design (Envoy extension for 5G SBI semantics)
key_result: Argues that off-the-shelf meshes lack 5G-specific semantics and proposes Envoy-based enhancements that map SCP-like indirect communication onto a service mesh.
limitation_or_critique: Largely conceptual with no quantitative evaluation of the proposed mesh enhancements or of AI-driven routing/selection policies.

title: Prospects on the adoption of a microservice-based architecture in 5G systems and beyond
authors: Sebastian Robitzsch; Marco Centenaro; Nicola di Pietro; Luis Cordeiro; André S. Gomes; Peter Sanders; Arif Ishaq
summary: Position/review paper arguing that the 5GC needs deeper re-design into true microservices and illustrating the decomposition of three example network functions into services with distinct responsibilities.
method: Architectural analysis and NF decomposition (theoretical and practical)
data_or_testbed: Prototype decomposition of example NFs (industrial partners, PREDICT-6G)
key_result: Shows that 3GPP NFs as specified remain coarse-grained and proposes a decomposition approach and directions for beyond-5G microservice cores.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on software architecture; scaling, NF selection and AI-driven orchestration of the resulting microservices are not evaluated.

title: A Review of Energy Information Collection and Exposure in 3GPP Mobile Networks
authors: Rashmi Kamran; Pranav Jha; Shwetha Kiran; Pradnya Taksande; Prasanna Chaporkar; Abhay Karandikar; Manjesh Hanawal
venue: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
summary: Reviews 3GPP Rel-19/20 work on energy-aware networks: collecting NF energy consumption, exposing it to users and application providers, and adjusting QoS to save energy.
method: standards review + policy mechanism proposal
key_result: Lists open problems of energy-aware 5G/6G design and proposes a new policy-update mechanism that uses energy information in the core.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference review with no quantitative evaluation of the proposed policy mechanism.

title: Energy-Efficient Softwarized Networks: A Survey
authors: Iwan Setiawan; Binayak Kar; Shan-Hsiang Shen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Surveys energy efficiency across SDN, NFV and network slicing, organising the literature by network scenario, control/MANO layer and energy-saving strategy.
method: systematic survey / taxonomy
key_result: Provides a comparative table of approaches, evaluation methods, criteria and metrics, showing that VNF deployment is the most studied energy lever in data-centre settings.
limitation_or_critique: Treats the mobile core only as one NFV scenario and does not map the reviewed techniques to 3GPP energy KPIs (TS 28.310) or Rel-19 energy-awareness work; first posted on arXiv in 2023 (2307.11301).

title: Energy-Aware 6G Network Design: A Survey
authors: Rashmi Kamran; Mahesh Ganesh Bhat; Pranav Jha; Shana Moothedath; Manjesh Hanawal; Prasanna Chaporkar
summary: Surveys methods for energy-aware 6G design, including energy models and parameters, classification of energy-aware services, energy harvesting, AI/ML solutions and 3GPP/ITU/IEEE standardisation.
method: survey
key_result: Identifies energy-information monitoring and exposure, renewable-energy awareness and user consent as the open design challenges for energy-aware services.
limitation_or_critique: Unrefereed preprint; broad scope means core-network NF-level energy optimisation is covered only at a conceptual level.

title: AI Models for Green Communications Towards 6G
authors: Bomin Mao; Fengxiao Tang; Yuichi Kawamoto; Nei Kato
summary: Surveys how machine-learning and deep-learning models are used to cut energy demand, raise energy efficiency and manage energy harvesting across 5G/6G communication scenarios.
method: survey
key_result: Argues that AI-based network management is the main path to reconcile 6G QoS and intelligence demands with energy targets, and catalogues ML techniques per scenario.
limitation_or_critique: Heavily oriented to radio, IoT and edge scenarios; core-network functions and 3GPP management-plane energy KPIs receive little attention.

title: A Survey on 5G Radio Access Network Energy Efficiency: Massive MIMO, Lean Carrier Design, Sleep Modes, and Machine Learning
authors: David Lopez-Perez; Antonio De Domenico; Nicola Piovesan; Geng Xinli; Harvey Bao; Song Qitao; Merouane Debbah
summary: Reviews power-consumption models, energy-efficiency metrics and the NR features (massive MIMO, lean carrier, advanced sleep modes, AI) that reduce RAN energy use.
method: survey
key_result: Shows that 3GPP NR already offers substantial built-in energy-saving tools whose optimal operation points depend on traffic-aware control.
limitation_or_critique: RAN-only by design; included as the reference energy survey because the RAN dominates energy literature, but it says nothing about core NFs.

title: Open the Floodgates in a Digital Twin: Experiences of Building Spillway for 100M+-User Signaling Storms in Cellular Core Network
authors: Hongtao Xie; Jianmin Liu; Ce Yang; Yu He; Li Chen; Dan Li; Mineng Fu; Xi Chen; Siyu Chen
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2026 Conference
summary: Describes Spillway, an operator-deployed digital-twin system that tunes overload-control parameters of core network elements against signalling storms by simulating candidate configurations before deployment.
method: Domain-specific vectorised discrete-event simulator (CN-DES) plus heteroscedastic evolutionary Bayesian optimisation
data_or_testbed: Production 5G SA core of a very large operator (five-year deployment)
key_result: CN-DES simulates regional storms with tens of millions of users in minutes (about 60x faster than conventional simulation) and optimised configurations reduced user fallbacks during real incidents.
limitation_or_critique: Rare at-scale evidence of DT-based what-if validation of core configuration, but the simulator is proprietary and tied to one operator's network, limiting reproducibility.

title: From Monitoring to Prediction: Hands-on Experience on Building a Cloud-Native Network Digital Twin for 5G Core
authors: Lanfranco Zanzi; Xi Li; Marco Liebsch; Fujita Satoshi; Datta Kalaswan; Sagara Mio
venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Presents a containerised monitoring-and-prediction pipeline that instantiates NDTs for performance management of a commercial 5G core, forecasting CPU and memory stress of core NFs from live telemetry.
method: Cloud-native telemetry ingestion with ML forecasting of NF resource KPIs
data_or_testbed: Commercial 5G core on Kubernetes in AWS under stress workloads
key_result: Reports accurate prediction of system degradation under stressing workloads and support for closed-loop control.
limitation_or_critique: The twin is essentially a KPI forecaster; fidelity for what-if analysis of configuration or topology changes is not demonstrated.

title: COREX: Framework for Distributed Digital Twins of 5G/6G Network Topologies and Automated Experiment Executions
authors: Pablo Benlloch-Caballero; Pablo Salva-Garcia; Qi Wang; Jose M. Alcaraz Calero
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Presents COREX, an automation framework that orchestrates emulated, distributed digital twins of 5G/6G topologies spanning access, edge, transport and core, and runs predefined experiments and cyber ranges.
method: Emulation-based DT orchestration with automated experiment execution
key_result: Setup time grows with UE count (roughly 700 to 1,200 s) and a self-protection closed loop that detects and mitigates threats was demonstrated.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation focuses on framework scalability and security loops; twin-to-reality fidelity and live synchronisation are not quantified.

title: Management and orchestration; Management aspects of Network Digital Twins
authors: 3GPP
venue: 3GPP TS 28.561 V19.3.0 (Rel-19); Rel-20 V20.2.0 in progress
summary: Normative SA5 specification that defines the NDT as a virtual replica of a mobile network or part of it and specifies NDT management services, lifecycle management and relations to network automation.
method: Standard (requirements, information model, management services)
key_result: First 3GPP normative basis for NDT lifecycle management, with Rel-20 phase 2 extending it to new use cases such as NTN.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies management of the twin, not how fidelity is achieved or validated, leaving model accuracy and synchronisation to implementations.

title: A Network Digital Twin of a 5G Private Network: Designing a Proof-of-Concept from Theory to Practice
authors: Cristina Emilia Costa; Tatenda Horiro Zhou; Fabrizio Granelli
summary: Reports a practical NDT deployment mirroring a laboratory 5G private network using open-source emulation software, released to the community.
method: Emulation-based NDT with physical-vs-twin measurement comparison
key_result: Measurements indicate the twin closely reproduces the state and behaviour of the physical network (no figures in the abstract).
limitation_or_critique: Small lab scale and unrefereed preprint; fidelity is shown for a single setup without what-if or closed-loop use.

title: Deep Learning-Based Modeling of 5G Core Control Plane for 5G Network Digital Twin
authors: Zhenyu Tao; Yongliang Guo; Guanghui He; Yongming Huang; Xiaohu You
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
summary: Builds data-driven twins of the 5G core control plane by learning signalling behaviour with sequence-to-sequence and Transformer-decoder models (5GC-Seq2Seq and 5GC-former).
method: Seq2Seq and Transformer models over vectorised NAS/NGAP signalling messages
data_or_testbed: Signalling traces from a Spirent C50 tester (registration, handover, PDU session)
key_result: The Transformer model exceeds 99.999% F1-score and stays robust with concurrent UEs, whereas the simpler Seq2Seq degrades under concurrency.
limitation_or_critique: Twin reproduces message sequences of a tester-driven core but not timing, load or NF resource behaviour, so its use for what-if capacity or failure analysis is untested.

title: Digital twin-assisted flexible slice admission control for 5G core network: A deep reinforcement learning approach
authors: Jiadai Wang; Jingyi Li; Jiajia Liu
summary: Proposes a DRL slice admission scheme for the 5G core that may partially admit slice requests via a scaling factor and trains the agent inside a digital twin to avoid disrupting the live network.
method: Deep reinforcement learning with DT-based training environment
key_result: Reported higher slice deployment revenue and acceptance ratio than baseline admission policies.
limitation_or_critique: The twin is a simulated environment for safe exploration rather than a synchronised replica, and evaluation is simulation-only without real core NFs.

title: Study on management aspect of Network Digital Twin
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA5 Rel-19 study on using NDTs in network management, collecting use cases (automation support, verification of changes, data generation) and potential solutions, and recommending normative work on NDT lifecycle management.
method: Technical report (use cases, potential solutions, conclusions)
key_result: Concluded that NDT instance lifecycle management should be standardised, leading to TS 28.561.
limitation_or_critique: Study-level only; positions the NDT as a tool used by automation functions rather than a replacement for closed loops, without performance requirements.

title: B5GEMINI: Digital Twin Network for 5G and Beyond
authors: Alberto Mozo; Amit Karamchandani; Mario Sanz; Jose Ignacio Moreno; Antonio Pastor
venue: NOMS 2022-2022 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Introduces B5GEMINI, an AI-centric digital twin network for 5G and beyond, describing its infrastructure and architectural components and five AI use cases built on it.
method: Architecture and use-case design of an emulation-based DTN
key_result: Identifies the AI ecosystem components (data generation, model training, validation) a 5G DTN must offer.
limitation_or_critique: Mostly architectural with use cases sketched rather than evaluated quantitatively.

title: Network Digital Twin for Route Optimization in 5G/B5G Transport Slicing with What-If Analysis
authors: Rebecca Aben-Athar; Heitor Anglada; Lucas Costa; João Albuquerque; Abrahão Ferreira; Cristiano Bonato Both; Kleber Cardoso; Silvia Lins; Andrey Silva; Glauco Gonçalves; Ilan Correa; Aldebaro Klautau
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
summary: Builds an experimental platform where a GNN-based NDT of the 5G/B5G transport network, synchronised with the physical side, feeds a recommender that performs what-if analysis for slice-aware route optimisation.
method: GNN performance model + recommendation system for what-if analysis
key_result: Latency predictions for URLLC and eMBB slices showed low MAPE against measured latency after applying the recommended routes.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper limited to the transport segment; core NFs and control-plane effects are outside the twin.

title: When Digital Twin Meets Generative AI: Intelligent Closed-Loop Network Management
authors: Xinyu Huang; Haojun Yang; Conghao Zhou; Mingcheng He; Xuemin Shen; Weihua Zhuang
summary: Proposes a generative-AI-driven digital twin architecture in which GAI models support status emulation, feature abstraction and decision-making for internal and external closed-loop network management.
method: Architecture proposal with data-model-driven management case study
key_result: Suggests model light-weighting, adaptive model selection and data-model-driven management to improve DT-based closed loops.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style vision with a single case study; no mapping to 3GPP closed-loop or NDT management services.

title: Generative Network Performance Prediction with Network Digital Twin
authors: Bilgehan Erman; Catello Di Martino
summary: Extends an operator NDT platform for private industrial 5G networks with DNN models linking field measurements to digital representations and GANs that generate what-if scenarios for SLA compliance prediction.
method: DNN mapping + GAN-based what-if scenario generation
data_or_testbed: Field measurements from industrial private wireless networks
key_result: Shows that generated what-if layouts and configurations can expose SLA risks before they occur in the physical network.
limitation_or_critique: Radio/coverage-centred and vendor-specific; the core network and its configuration are not part of the twin.

title: Network Digital Twin (NDT): Concepts and Reference Architecture
authors: IRTF NMRG
venue: IRTF NMRG Internet-Draft draft-irtf-nmrg-network-digital-twin-arch-13 (Informational, work in progress)
summary: Research-group draft giving NDT definitions, a reference architecture with data, model and interface building blocks, application scenarios and key challenges.
method: Informational reference architecture
key_result: Most mature IETF/IRTF NDT reference architecture, past RG last call and awaiting IRTF chair processing.
limitation_or_critique: Technology-agnostic IP-network view with no 3GPP core specifics; not a standard and still a draft.

title: Digital twin network - Requirements and architecture
authors: ITU-T SG13
summary: ITU-T Recommendation specifying functional and service requirements, a functional architecture and security considerations for digital twin networks.
method: Standard (requirements and architecture)
key_result: Defines a DTN as a virtual counterpart enabling analysis, diagnosis, emulation and control of the physical network through data, models and interfaces.
limitation_or_critique: High-level and network-agnostic; does not address mobile-core functions or how DTN outputs are validated before actuation.

title: Toward AI-Native 6G Systems: Standards Enablers for 6G Network Automation
authors: Sayantini Majumdar; Qing Wei; Susanna Schwarzmann; Riccardo Trivisonno; Georg Carle
summary: Argues that the 5G AI-overlay model (NWDAF as an add-on queried by NFs) limits autonomy and proposes 6G standards enablers where each NF embeds an intelligent agent coordinated by an AI controller (INTDAI).
method: architectural proposal / standards analysis
key_result: Introduces an integrated distributed AI automation layer with AI data and AI control enablers as a path from overlay analytics to native AI in 6G.
limitation_or_critique: Vision-style magazine article whose benefits are illustrated on a single use case rather than measured on a testbed.

title: Architecture enhancements for 5G System (5GS) to support network data analytics services
authors: 3GPP
summary: Stage-2 specification of NWDAF: architecture, AnLF/MTLF split, data collection via DCCF/ADRF/MFAF, federated learning among NWDAFs, and the full catalogue of analytics IDs (NF load, QoS sustainability, abnormal behaviour, etc.).
method: standard (stage 2 architecture)
key_result: Defines the normative analytics IDs, procedures and ML-model provisioning/accuracy monitoring that research prototypes are expected to comply with.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies interfaces and procedures but deliberately leaves algorithms, training data quality and performance targets to implementations.

title: Towards zero-touch network orchestration: An NWDAF-centered standards-compliant closed-loop approach
authors: Fatemeh Shafiei Ardestani; Noura Limam; Raouf Boutaba
venue: ITU Journal on Future and Evolving Technologies
summary: Presents a standards-compliant closed-loop framework that turns NWDAF into an active runtime orchestration component, with a UPF event exposure service, modular analytics engines with ML lifecycle management, and policy enforcement via control-plane NFs.
method: closed-loop NWDAF framework; ML lifecycle (MLflow)
key_result: Fine-grained user-plane telemetry is collected with small overhead and enables anomaly mitigation and congestion-aware QoS adaptation at runtime.
limitation_or_critique: Journal extension of the NOMS 2026 paper (10.1109/NOMS69089.2026.11668240); evaluated on two lab use cases rather than at operator scale.

title: Agentic-NWDAF: Enabling Intent-driven Agentic Intelligence for Autonomous 6G Network Analytics
authors: Mazene Ameur; Bouziane Brik; Adlen Ksentini
venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Adds an intent-aware agentic orchestration layer that translates natural-language OSS intents into NWDAF service calls using collaborating LLM agents and the Model Context Protocol.
method: LLM multi-agent system; MCP
data_or_testbed: benchmark of 100 NWDAF intents derived from 3GPP specs
key_result: Authors report high accuracy and good generalisation on their intent benchmark judged with an LLM-as-a-judge method.
limitation_or_critique: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation on a self-built benchmark leaves correctness, latency and safety of generated NWDAF calls only partly validated.

title: Enhanced Open-Source NWDAF for Event-Driven Analytics in 5G Networks
authors: Henok Daniel; Omar Alhussein; Jie Liang; Cheng Li; Ernesto Damiani
summary: Builds an open-source NWDAF integrated with free5GC, adding event subscription/notification support in SMF and AMF and a mobility module that predicts the next handover cell.
method: event exposure extensions; ML handover-cell prediction
data_or_testbed: free5GC with 4 virtual gNBs and virtual UEs (two-week run)
key_result: Next-gNB handover prediction reached about 81% accuracy (80.65%) in the two-week emulated deployment.
limitation_or_critique: Preprint evaluated on emulated UEs and gNBs only, with a single mobility analytics use case.

title: Fair Federated Learning for Multi-Task 6G NWDAF Network Anomaly Detection
authors: Chunjiong Zhang; Gaoyang Shan; Byeong-Hee Roh
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
summary: Applies fair federated learning to the 3GPP NWDAF architecture with a multi-task model detecting traffic anomalies of different device types, optimised via alternating gradient projection.
method: fair FL; multi-task learning; alternating gradient projection
key_result: The multi-task FL model detects anomalies for several device types at once and outperforms compared baselines in simulation.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only evaluation with no deployment on a 5G core, and venue (transportation systems) is outside the core-networking community.

title: A Protocol-Based Framework for AIaaS Lifecycle Management in 6G via NWDAF
authors: Júnia Maísa Oliveira; Daniel Fernandes Macedo; José Marcos NogueiraIEEE
venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Proposes an enhanced NWDAF acting as an AI-as-a-Service lifecycle manager with model orchestrator, registry/validator, execution engine and feedback aggregator plus two new service-based protocols for training and execution.
method: protocol design; formal verification (TLA+)
key_result: Formal verification under message loss and complexity modelling indicate linear resource scaling up to 128 NFs.
limitation_or_critique: Validated by formal model checking and theoretical scaling only, with no prototype in a 5G core.

title: SAMMF: A Self-Adaptive Multi-Model Fusion Framework for NWDAF Traffic Anomaly Detection
authors: Mingchuang Zhang; Hongbo Tang; Jie Yang; Hang Qiu; Yu Zhao; Mingyan Xu; Yi Bai
summary: Proposes an NWDAF framework that adaptively selects high-performing models from a library per NF data source and fuses their outputs for anomaly traffic detection.
method: adaptive model selection + multi-model fusion
data_or_testbed: two public network anomaly detection datasets
key_result: Outperforms baseline single models in handling heterogeneous NF data for anomaly detection.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on generic intrusion datasets rather than data collected from 5G core NFs.

title: Study on Core Network Enhanced Support for Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML)
authors: 3GPP
summary: Rel-19 SA2 study on core network AI/ML enhancements, including vertical federated learning between NWDAF and AF, AI/ML-assisted positioning and QoS/policy, and new analytics such as abnormal signalling detection.
method: standard (study report)
key_result: Lists key issues and candidate solutions that fed the Rel-19 NWDAF normative work (e.g., VFL, accuracy and trust of analytics).
limitation_or_critique: Study-phase report: many solutions are alternatives without conclusions or quantitative evaluation.

title: Real-Time Monitoring of 5G Networks: An NWDAF and ML Based KPI Prediction
authors: Abebu Ademe Bayleyegn; Zaloa Fernández; Fabrizio Granelli
venue: 2024 IEEE 10th International Conference on Network Softwarization (NetSoft)
summary: Builds a real-time monitoring solution for the 5G SBA around an in-house NWDAF and extends it with ML models predicting traffic KPIs, exporting metrics to Prometheus/Grafana.
method: ML KPI forecasting; observability stack
key_result: Demonstrates standardised NWDAF-based monitoring with integrated KPI prediction on a running 5G core.
limitation_or_critique: Prediction accuracy and scalability are evaluated only on a lab testbed and the analytics are not fed back into control actions.

title: Enhancing Network Data Analytics Functions: Integrating AIaaS with ML Model Provisioning
authors: Ali Nadar; Jérôme Härri
venue: 2024 22nd Mediterranean Communication and Computer Networking Conference (MedComNet)
summary: Extends the OpenAirInterface NWDAF toward a Rel-17 architecture with AI/ML model sharing through APIs to an external AI-as-a-Service platform and an AI/ML ontology.
method: MTLF-style model provisioning; ontology
key_result: Demonstrates feasibility of ML model sharing between NWDAF and an AIaaS platform on an abnormal-traffic-behaviour use case.
limitation_or_critique: Feasibility demo without performance metrics for model transfer latency, accuracy or multi-vendor interoperability.

title: Model Drift in Dynamic Networks
authors: Dimitrios Michael Manias; Ali Chouman; Abdallah Shami
summary: Discusses types of model drift threatening ML models deployed in 5G networks and proposes a drift detection and adaptation framework illustrated with a 5G core case study.
method: drift detection/adaptation framework
key_result: Shows that emulated changes in user behaviour degrade deployed models and that a detection-plus-adaptation loop can trigger remediation.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-level treatment; the companion MeditCom 2022 paper (10.1109/MeditCom55741.2022.9928667) holds the core-specific framework and evaluation, both on small emulated testbeds.

title: Combining Network Data Analytics Function and Machine Learning for Abnormal Traffic Detection in Beyond 5G
authors: Abdelkader Mekrache; Karim Boutiba; Adlen Ksentini
summary: Proposes a microservice-based NWDAF architecture and integrates an LSTM autoencoder for abnormal traffic detection with the OpenAirInterface 5G core and RAN.
method: LSTM autoencoder; microservice NWDAF
key_result: Shows end-to-end 3GPP-compliant data collection from a real 5G core and detection of abnormal traffic generated by a real UE.
limitation_or_critique: Training relies on the Milano telecom dataset rather than core-native data, and the evaluation is a single-use-case lab demo.

title: Securing Federated Learning Enabled NWDAF Architecture With Partial Homomorphic Encryption
authors: Changshi Zhou; Nirwan Ansari
summary: Proposes a federated-learning-enabled multi-NWDAF architecture where model updates shared among NWDAFs are protected with partial homomorphic encryption.
method: federated learning + Paillier-style partial HE
key_result: Simulation indicates the encrypted FL model sharing among NWDAFs is feasible while preserving data privacy.
limitation_or_critique: Letter-length simulation study with no integration into a 5G core and limited analysis of encryption overhead at scale.

title: Towards Supporting Intelligence in 5G/6G Core Networks: NWDAF Implementation and Initial Analysis
authors: Ali Chouman; Dimitrios Michael Manias; Abdallah Shami
venue: 2022 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
summary: Integrates a functional NWDAF into an open-source 5G core and analyses the NF interaction data it collects, outlining how the insights could drive intelligent network management.
method: prototype NWDAF + exploratory data analysis
key_result: Demonstrates practical NWDAF data collection over SBA interfaces and the type of NF-interaction insights it yields.
limitation_or_critique: Initial analysis without a deployed ML model or closed loop, on a small-scale emulated network.

title: An NWDAF Approach to 5G Core Network Signaling Traffic: Analysis and Characterization
authors: Dimitrios Michael Manias; Ali Chouman; Abdallah Shami
summary: Uses an NWDAF prototype on a working 5G core to collect control-plane signaling data and characterises intra-core NF interactions with unsupervised clustering.
method: unsupervised learning (clustering)
key_result: Clustering of NWDAF-collected signaling exposes distinct NF interaction patterns usable for proactive load balancing.
limitation_or_critique: Characterisation study only; the identified clusters are not yet used for a control decision or validated on operator traffic.

title: A Distributed NWDAF Architecture for Federated Learning in 5G
authors: Youbin Jeon; Hyeonjae Jeong; Sangwon Seo; Taeyun Kim; Haneul Ko; Sangheon Pack
venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
summary: Introduces a hierarchical NWDAF structure in which leaf NWDAFs train local models and a root NWDAF aggregates them by federated learning.
method: hierarchical federated learning
key_result: Argues the leaf/root design reduces analytics-data transfer and central overload while keeping data local.
limitation_or_critique: Consumer-electronics conference short paper with a conceptual architecture and limited quantitative evaluation.

title: Ensemble Learning-based Network Data Analytics for Network Slice Orchestration and Management: An Intent-Based Networking Mechanism
authors: Khizar Abbas; Talha Ahmed Khan; Muhammad Afaq; Wang-Cheol Song
venue: NOMS 2022-2022 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Combines an intent-based networking platform for end-to-end slice orchestration with NWDAF-style ensemble-learning analytics for resource-utilisation prediction and anomaly detection in a closed loop.
method: stacking ensemble learning; IBN closed loop
key_result: Stacking ensemble improved resource-utilisation prediction accuracy by up to about 20% and cut error by 45% versus baselines.
limitation_or_critique: Analytics are only loosely mapped to 3GPP NWDAF services and gains are shown on a limited dataset.

title: Intelligent network data analytics function in 5G cellular networks using machine learning
authors: Salih Sevgican; Meric Turan; Kerim Gokarslan; H. Birkan Yilmaz; Tuna Tugcu
summary: Describes the NWDAF structure and protocols and evaluates ML models (linear regression, LSTM, RNN, logistic regression, XGBoost) for load prediction and anomaly classification on a 3GPP-field-based synthetic cell dataset.
method: LSTM/RNN regression, XGBoost classification
key_result: Neural sequence models gave the best load prediction and gradient boosting the best anomaly classification among the compared models.
limitation_or_critique: Early and widely cited but relies on synthetic data with injected anomalies and does not run inside a real 5G core or NWDAF implementation.

title: Management and orchestration; Management Data Analytics (MDA)
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA5 specification of management-plane analytics (MDA): MDA functionality and service framework, MDA capabilities and use cases (coverage, fault, slice, energy), and the role of ML in MDA.
method: standard (management analytics)
key_result: Defines MDA requests/reports and use cases complementing control-plane NWDAF analytics within the management loop.
limitation_or_critique: Management-plane focus with few academic implementations, so its interplay with NWDAF remains largely unevaluated.

title: Revamping the Resilience and High Availability of 5G Core for 6G Ready Network Slices
authors: Shwetha Vittal; Sourav Sarkar; A. Antony Franklin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Builds a self-resilient 5GC that combines column-generation ILP scheduling of control-plane requests per slice with an LSTM predicting the availability of NF serving instances inside a closed loop.
method: column generation ILP + LSTM availability prediction in closed-loop SON
key_result: Under overload and instance failures it drops about 15% fewer requests in delay-tolerant and 5% fewer in delay-sensitive slices than prior schemes, with LSTM accuracy around 95%.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on a small testbed cluster; geo-distributed failures and alignment with 3GPP NF set / restoration procedures are not examined.

title: RECAP 5GC: Resilience and CAP aware 5G Core for Consistent and High Availability Service
authors: Siddhesh Pratim Sovitkar; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
venue: NOMS 2024-2024 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Designs a CAP-aware 5GC that keeps UE state consistent and the service available during sudden failures of stateless NFs, implemented between AMF and UDSF in an active/active cluster.
method: CAP-aware state handling between AMF and UDSF, active/active HA
key_result: Drops 47% fewer requests than CP mode and 86% fewer than AP mode while being 1.6% more available than CP mode and staying consistent.
limitation_or_critique: Limited to the AMF-UDSF pair on a two-node cluster; WAN partitions between geo-redundant sites are not tested (builds on the CCNC 2024 CAP study by the same group).

title: CoreKube: An Efficient, Autoscaling and Resilient Mobile Core System
authors: Jon Larrea; Andrew E. Ferguson; Mahesh K. Marina
venue: Proceedings of the 29th Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking
summary: Message-focused cloud-native mobile core with fully stateless generic workers, a shared state database and a RAN-facing frontend, orchestrated by Kubernetes for autoscaling and self-healing.
method: stateless worker architecture with externalised state on Kubernetes
key_result: Processes control-plane messages efficiently, scales with few resources and recovers seamlessly from failures relative to prior cores.
limitation_or_critique: Recovery relies on Kubernetes self-healing and a single shared database whose own replication/geo-redundancy is not the focus; departs from the standard per-NF SBA decomposition.

title: Failure Prediction in Cloud Native 5G Core With eBPF-based Observability
authors: Junichi Kawasaki; Daiki Koyama; Takuya Miyasaka; Tomohiro Otani
summary: Collects fine-grained infrastructure telemetry with eBPF and trains an LSTM to forecast KPI evolution for proactive failure prediction in a cloud-native 5GC.
method: eBPF observability + LSTM KPI forecasting
key_result: The LSTM trained with eBPF-derived features predicts future KPI transitions better than models trained without them.
limitation_or_critique: Lab-only with limited fault types; no link to automated recovery actions or to NWDAF-based analytics exposure.

title: Towards zero downtime: Using machine learning to predict network failure in 5G and beyond
authors: Emmanuel Basikolo; Thomas Basikolo
venue: ITU Journal on Future and Evolving Technologies
summary: Trains supervised regressors on observability data from a CNF-based 5GC testbed to predict whether a network failure will occur within the next ten minutes.
method: random forest, gradient boosting, SVR (proposed tuned SVR)
data_or_testbed: 5GC CNF testbed observability dataset (ITU AI/ML in 5G challenge)
key_result: The proposed SVR predicts failure events ten minutes ahead with an F1-score above 0.9.
limitation_or_critique: Single dataset and classical models, with no deployment loop or explanation of failure causes.

title: HARNESS: High Availability Supportive Self Reliant Network Slicing in 5G Networks
authors: Shwetha Vittal; A. Antony Franklin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Proposes a SON-driven high-availability slicing system for the 5GC that schedules control-plane user service requests across delay-tolerant and delay-sensitive slices under overload and scaling events.
method: self-organising scheduling algorithms with XDP/eBPF dataplane
key_result: Reduces blocking of critical control-plane requests by 60% and their average response time by 50%, with about 3.2% higher slice availability in a two-node cluster.
limitation_or_critique: Availability gains are shown on a minimal two-node cluster; no ML model and no evaluation of site-level (geo) failures.

title: Automatic failover of 5G container-based User Plane Function by ONAP closed-loop orchestration
authors: Akos Leiter; Attila Hegyi; Nandor Galambosi; Edina Lami; Peter Fazekas
venue: NOMS 2022-2022 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Demonstrates inter-cluster failover of a containerised 5G UPF triggered automatically by an ONAP closed control loop.
method: ONAP closed-loop automation for CNF failover
data_or_testbed: ONAP with Kubernetes clusters and containerised UPF
key_result: Shows that a closed-loop orchestrator can detect UPF failure and re-establish the user plane in another cluster without manual intervention.
limitation_or_critique: Short demo-style paper with limited quantitative evaluation of failover time and session continuity.

title: System Failure Prediction within Software 5G Core Networks using Time Series Forecasting
authors: Pousali Chakraborty; Marius Corici; Thomas Magedanz
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
summary: Integrates time-series analytics into a software 5G core to forecast conditions that can lead to system failures.
method: time-series forecasting on core monitoring data
key_result: Shows feasibility of forecasting threats to 5GC stability from monitored load metrics within the core.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper with a narrow evaluation; later work by the same group (FNWF 2025, Globecom Wkshps 2025) extends it with outlier-density and nonlinear-dynamics analysis.

title: Making cellular networks crisis-proof: Towards island-ready, resilient-by-design 6G communication networks
authors: Leon Janzen; Matthias Hollick
summary: Position/analysis paper arguing that the centralised 5G core makes cellular service fragile under disasters and proposing island-ready 6G networks that keep local connectivity and services when cut off from the core.
method: conceptual analysis and readiness assessment of 5G/5G-Advanced
key_result: Evaluates the island readiness of 5G and 5G-Advanced systems and lists open challenges such as decentralising the 6G core and local-first application design.
limitation_or_critique: Vision-oriented with no quantitative availability analysis; the companion IFIP Networking 2026 paper (10.23919/ifipnetworking70592.2026.11579031) provides the lab prototype.

title: 5G System; Restoration procedures
authors: 3GPP
summary: Stage-2 specification of 5GS restoration: N4/UPF/SMF failure and restart detection, path failure, NF and NF-service failure handling over SBI, AMF and NG-RAN failure, UDM/AUSF data restoration.
method: standard
key_result: Defines how peers detect NF restarts and recover sessions/contexts, including selection of alternative NF instances after a failure.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies mechanisms but no availability targets, failure-prediction or AI-assisted recovery; Rel-20 V20.0.0 (2026-06) exists.

title: TEGRA: A Flexible & Scalable NextGen Mobile Core
authors: Bilal Saleem; Omar Basit; Jiayi Meng; Iftekhar Alam; Ajay Thakur; Christian Maciocco; Muhammad Shahbaz; Y. Charlie Hu; Larry Peterson
summary: Presents an SBA-based mobile core with resilient microservice design patterns and state-management strategies, supporting multiple instances per service for failover.
method: resilient SBA microservice patterns and state management
data_or_testbed: comparison with free5GC, Open5GS, Aether, CoreKube
key_result: Processes requests about 20x faster than free5GC and 11x faster than Open5GS while matching CoreKube performance.
limitation_or_critique: Preprint not yet peer reviewed; resilience mechanisms are described but availability is not quantified in the abstract.

title: Availability and Reliability of Core Networks (4G/5G) From a Deployment Standpoint
authors: Priyatosh Mandal
summary: Derives analytical availability and reliability of 4G/5G core network services deployed as VNFs, comparing placement of all core nodes in a single VM versus multiple VMs with host, VM and NF failures.
method: analytical availability/reliability modelling
key_result: Single-VM deployment yields more than 14% higher availability and more than 100% higher reliability than multi-VM deployment under the model assumptions.
limitation_or_critique: VM-centric model without container/Kubernetes recovery, NF redundancy or geo-redundancy, and no empirical validation.

title: Performability Management of 5G Service Chains with Rejuvenation: The Open5GS Use Case
authors: L. De Simone; M. Di Mauro; M. Longo; R. Natella; F. Postiglione
venue: 2025 IEEE 11th International Conference on Network Softwarization (NetSoft)
summary: Stochastic performability framework for 5G service chains combining an M/G/m latency model with stochastic reward nets that include software rejuvenation, used to pick 5G settings meeting delay and five-nines targets.
method: M/G/m queueing + stochastic reward networks with rejuvenation
data_or_testbed: Open5GS testbed for parameter estimation and validation
key_result: Identifies the minimal 5GC configurations that jointly satisfy a latency threshold and five-nines availability, validated on Open5GS.
limitation_or_critique: Exponential/steady-state assumptions and testbed-estimated parameters; the group extends it to multi-tenant (RNDM 2024) and non-exponential transient models (NetSoft 2026).

title: Design of Resilient Mobile Core Network Architecture Inspired by Soft Guarantee Behavior
authors: Masayuki Kurata; Ryu Watanabe; Masaki Suzuki
venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Proposes SG-MCN, a core architecture that keeps authentication, authorisation and session setup working during data-tier outages using precomputed vectors and cached per-device contexts while staying 3GPP-security compliant.
method: soft-guarantee speculative processing bypassing data-tier NFs
key_result: Sustains QoE scores close to the normal core even when data-tier functions are unavailable.
limitation_or_critique: Emulation-based; speculative authorisation raises consistency/security trade-offs that need operator validation.

title: Neutrino: A Fast and Consistent Edge-Based Cellular Control Plane
authors: Mukhtiar Ahmad; Syed Muhammad Nawazish Ali; Muhammad Taimoor Tariq; Syed Usman Jafri; Adnan Abbas; Syeda Mashal Abbas Zaidi; Muhammad Basit Iqbal Awan; Zartash Afzal Uzmi; Zafar Ayyub Qazi
summary: Designs an edge-based cellular control plane that provides reliable, consistent access to control services with lower procedure completion times, including under control-plane failures.
method: edge-distributed control plane with consistent state replication
data_or_testbed: testbed driven by real cellular control traffic traces
key_result: Improves control procedure completion times by up to 3.1x without failures and up to 5.6x under control-plane failures compared with existing 5G.
limitation_or_critique: Requires non-standard changes to the control-plane design; interaction with 3GPP restoration procedures and NF sets is not discussed.

title: ML-SLD: A message-level stateless design for cloud-native 5G core network
authors: Keliang Du; Luhan Wang; Xiangming Wen; Yu Liu; Haiwen Niu; Shaoxin Huang
summary: Proposes a message-level stateless 5GC with servitised N2 connectivity and on-demand message forwarding to shield RAN connections and users from cloud fluctuations and NF failures.
method: message-level stateless design, N2 servitisation, on-demand forwarding
data_or_testbed: OAI 5GC on Kubernetes; UERANSIM; Chaosblade fault injection
key_result: Prototype experiments with chaos-style fault injection show the design maintains RAN-core connectivity and reduces the impact of cloud fluctuations versus a stateful baseline.
limitation_or_critique: Single-cluster prototype; consistency of the external state store and geo-distribution are not quantified.

title: Procedure-Aware Stateless Systems for 5G & Beyond Core Networks
authors: Endri Goshi; Vignesh Karunakaran; Hasanin Harkous; Rastin Pries; Wolfgang Kellerer
summary: Reduces the cost of state externalisation in a stateless 5GC with piggyback-based and proactive-push state transfer tailored to the structure of control procedures.
method: procedure-aware state transfer (piggyback, proactive push)
key_result: Piggybacking cuts completion time of two synchronous procedures by about 44% and 70%, and proactive push improves asynchronous ones by 13-22%, without extra CPU or bandwidth.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on latency of stateless operation; failover time and state loss under actual NF failures are not measured.

title: L25GC: A Low Latency 5G Core Network based on High-Performance NFV Platforms
authors: Vivek Jain; Hao-Tse Chu; Shixiong Qi; Chia-An Lee; Hung-Cheng Chang; Cheng-Ying Hsieh; K. K. Ramakrishnan; Jyh-Cheng Chen
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2022 Conference
summary: Re-architects free5GC around shared-memory NFV to cut control-plane latency and adds integrated failure resiliency that recovers NF and hardware failures transparently.
method: shared-memory NFV 5GC with built-in failure resiliency
key_result: Recovers from 5GC NF and hardware failures much faster than the 3GPP re-attach procedure and roughly halves event completion time for several control-plane events.
limitation_or_critique: Resiliency is one feature of a latency-oriented design; the prototype supports a limited number of sessions (addressed in L25GC+, CloudNet 2023).

title: The Cost of Stateless Network Functions in 5G
authors: Umakant Kulkarni; Amit Sheoran; Sonia Fahmy
venue: Proceedings of the Symposium on Architectures for Networking and Communications Systems
summary: Quantifies the latency cost of implementing 5G NFs statelessly with external state and compares several state-management paradigms and optimisations.
method: experimental comparison of state-management paradigms
key_result: Sharing user state among NFs reduces the statelessness overhead by about 10% on average; non-blocking calls and custom DB APIs help less.
limitation_or_critique: Preliminary short study; it measures cost but not the resilience benefit (recovery time, availability) that motivates statelessness.

title: Network Functions Virtualisation (NFV); Reliability; Report on Models and Features for End-to-End Reliability
authors: ETSI ISG NFV
summary: Reports models and features for end-to-end reliability of NFV network services, including redundancy schemes and reliability estimation.
method: standard (report)
key_result: Provides reference E2E reliability models that the availability-modelling literature on virtualised cores builds on.
limitation_or_critique: Pre-5GC (2016); no treatment of container orchestration or stateless SBA designs.

title: Network Functions Virtualisation (NFV); Resiliency Requirements
authors: ETSI ISG NFV
summary: Defines resiliency requirements for virtualised networks covering failure detection, migration, failure prediction and remediation of VNFs and NFVI.
method: standard
key_result: Sets baseline requirements such as transparent failover on NFVI failures that later availability models reference.
limitation_or_critique: Pre-5GC (2015) and VM-centric; does not cover cloud-native CNFs or 3GPP SBA restoration.

title: DT-LNS: Digital-Twin-Based Low-Risk Network Slicing Using Safe Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jin Li; Min Zhang; Qi Zhang; Danshi Wang
summary: Combines a DNN digital twin with uncertainty estimation and safe RL so that candidate slicing actions are pre-checked in the twin for SLA-violation risk before execution.
method: Safe RL with uncertainty-aware DNN digital twin
key_result: Keeps a high SLA satisfaction rate, reduces performance jitter and converges faster than six classic and RL-based slicing configuration methods.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only evaluation; the twin's uncertainty calibration under real traffic drift and core network failures is not tested.

title: ML-based 5G Core Network Load Forecasting With Metrics From Performance Management
authors: Tse-Ming Chen; Chien Chen; Jyh-Cheng Chen
venue: NOMS 2024-2024 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Collects performance-management measurements from an open-source 5G core and trains neural networks to forecast NF load, with a loss function tailored to the resource scaling policy.
method: Neural network load forecasting with scaling-aware loss
data_or_testbed: free5GC-based 5G core testbed with PM data
key_result: Adding performance-management measurements as inputs improves load prediction accuracy and supports scaling decisions.
limitation_or_critique: Single open-source testbed with synthetic signalling load; no comparison with NWDAF-standard analytics outputs or production traces.

title: Deep learning based resource forecasting for 5G core network scaling in Kubernetes environment
authors: Menuka Perera Jayasuriya Kuranage; Loutfi Nuaymi; Ahmed Bouabdallah; Thomas Ferrandiz; Philippe Bertin
venue: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Network Softwarization (NetSoft)
summary: Proposes deep-learning forecasting of containerised 5G core network function resource usage to drive proactive scaling decisions in Kubernetes.
method: Deep learning time-series forecasting (recurrent models)
data_or_testbed: Kubernetes testbed generating a 5G core resource usage dataset
key_result: The selected model gives accurate resource forecasts over longer horizons than a competing deep-learning forecasting approach.
limitation_or_critique: Forecasting is evaluated on testbed-generated traffic rather than operator traces, and the closed-loop scaling benefit is not quantified end to end.

title: A Graph Neural Network-Based Digital Twin for Network Slicing Management
authors: Haozhe Wang; Yulei Wu; Geyong Min; Wang Miao
summary: Builds a scalable digital twin of a slicing-enabled 5G network in which a GNN captures interactions among slices and predicts their end-to-end latency.
method: Graph neural network digital twin of network slices
data_or_testbed: Simulated slicing-enabled networks with varied topologies
key_result: The twin mirrors network behaviour and predicts slice end-to-end latency accurately under topologies and environments not seen in training.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation is simulation-based and abstracts the core network as graph nodes, without real NF telemetry or alignment with 3GPP slice management interfaces.

title: Machine Learning based Performance Prediction for Cloud-native 5G Mobile Core Network
authors: Shiku Hirai; Hiroki Baba; Minoru Matsumoto; Takafumi Hamano; Kento Noguchi
venue: 2022 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (WCNC)
summary: Builds ML models that predict the performance of cloud-native 5G core control-plane and user-plane functions from hardware resource features, as the basis of an automated CNF provisioning engine.
method: Supervised ML regression on CNF performance profiles
data_or_testbed: Operator test platform running a cloud-native 5G core
key_result: Models predict CNF performance with high accuracy using features that can be fed back directly into hardware resource design.
limitation_or_critique: Profiling is static and testbed-specific, and the paper does not address dynamic load, multi-tenant interference or online retraining.

title: OnSlicing: Online End-to-End Network Slicing with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Qiang Liu; Nakjung Choi; Tao Han
venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on emerging Networking EXperiments and Technologies
summary: Online end-to-end slicing system that uses constraint-aware DRL policy updates, proactive baseline switching and action modification to minimise resources without violating slice SLAs or infrastructure limits.
method: Constrained (safe) deep reinforcement learning with imitation warm-start
data_or_testbed: End-to-end testbed: OpenAirInterface 4G/5G RAN, OpenDayLight transport, core and edge
key_result: Learns online on a real testbed while keeping SLA violations low, thanks to constraint-aware updates and switching to a rule-based baseline.
limitation_or_critique: Core domain is handled by a simple resource manager on an LTE-era core, and scalability beyond a small testbed is not shown.

title: Mobile Network Traffic Prediction Using Temporal Fusion Transformer
authors: Georgios Kougioumtzidis; Vladimir K. Poulkov; Pavlos I. Lazaridis; Zaharias D. Zaharis
summary: Customises a temporal fusion transformer for multivariate mobile network traffic forecasting to support QoS-aware resource planning.
method: Temporal fusion transformer
key_result: The customised transformer beats state-of-the-art forecasting baselines in capturing the temporal dynamics of cellular traffic.
limitation_or_critique: Single-dataset evaluation of cell traffic with no link to core network decisions or to standardised analytics consumers.

title: MobiGPT: A Foundation Model for Mobile Wireless Networks
authors: Xiaoqian Qi; Haoye Chai; Yong Li
summary: Proposes a foundation model that forecasts base-station traffic, user app usage and channel quality with one architecture using soft prompts and temporal masking.
method: Foundation model with soft-prompt learning and temporal masking
data_or_testbed: Real-world mobile datasets with over 100,000 samples
key_result: Reports forecasting accuracy gains of roughly 7-27% over existing models and over 21% improvement in zero/few-shot unseen scenarios.
limitation_or_critique: Unreviewed preprint whose data are RAN/user-side; core network KPIs and deployment cost are not considered.

title: m3: Accurate Flow-Level Performance Estimation using Machine Learning
authors: Chenning Li; Arash Nasr-Esfahany; Kevin Zhao; Kimia Noorbakhsh; Prateesh Goyal; Mohammad Alizadeh; Thomas E. Anderson
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2024 Conference
summary: m3 decomposes network-wide estimation into sampled path-level problems, summarises each path workload with a fast fluid simulation and corrects it with a learned model.
method: Fluid simulation + ML correction on sampled paths
key_result: Reported as 5.7 times faster and with 45.9% less error than the Parsimon baseline for tail-latency estimation.
limitation_or_critique: Designed for data-center flow completion time estimation and has not been evaluated on mobile or core network workloads.

title: NetLLM: Adapting Large Language Models for Networking
authors: Duo Wu; Xianda Wang; Yaqi Qiao; Zhi Wang; Junchen Jiang; Shuguang Cui; Fangxin Wang
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2024 Conference
summary: Framework that adapts a pretrained LLM to networking prediction and decision tasks via multimodal encoders, task-specific output heads and low-cost domain fine-tuning.
method: LLM adaptation (multimodal encoder, networking head, efficient fine-tuning)
data_or_testbed: Viewport prediction, adaptive bitrate streaming and cluster job scheduling datasets
key_result: A single adapted LLM outperforms task-specific state-of-the-art algorithms on all three tasks and generalises better to unseen environments.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on application-level tasks only; inference cost and suitability for real-time core network control loops remain open questions.

title: RouteNet-Fermi: Network Modeling With Graph Neural Networks
authors: Miquel Ferriol-Galmés; Jordi Paillisse; José Suárez-Varela; Krzysztof Rusek; Shihan Xiao; Xiang Shi; Xiangle Cheng; Pere Barlet-Ros; Albert Cabellos-Aparicio
summary: Extends RouteNet into a GNN that targets the same outputs as queuing theory but handles non-Markovian traffic, mixed traffic profiles and arbitrary queue scheduling configurations.
method: Graph neural network with flow, queue and link states
data_or_testbed: Simulated datasets up to 300 nodes plus measurements from a physical testbed
key_result: Reaches about 6.2% mean relative delay error on topologies an order of magnitude larger than those seen during training, close to packet-level simulator accuracy at far lower cost.
limitation_or_critique: Journal successor of RouteNet-Erlang (INFOCOM 2022); still models IP forwarding queues rather than signalling-driven core network function performance.

title: Citywide Mobile Traffic Forecasting Using Spatial-Temporal Downsampling Transformer Neural Networks
authors: Yahui Hu; Yujiang Zhou; Junping Song; Luyang Xu; Xu Zhou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Proposes STD-Net, a transformer that splits a city into patches and uses a downsampling transformer to capture temporal, local and global spatial dependencies of mobile traffic at low cost.
method: Spatial-temporal transformer with downsampling
key_result: Outperforms state-of-the-art spatio-temporal baselines in citywide prediction accuracy while reducing spatial computational complexity.
limitation_or_critique: Predicts aggregate cell-level traffic volumes, which are an indirect proxy for core network function load.

title: Building a Digital Twin for network optimization using Graph Neural Networks
