authors: Miquel Ferriol-Galmés; José Suárez-Varela; Jordi Paillissé; Xiang Shi; Shihan Xiao; Xiangle Cheng; Pere Barlet-Ros; Albert Cabellos-Aparicio
summary: Proposes TwinNet, a GNN-based network digital twin that learns how queueing policy, topology, routing and traffic matrix jointly determine SLA metrics and uses it inside an optimisation loop.
method: Graph neural network digital twin
data_or_testbed: Synthetic simulation datasets validated with real traffic traces; 106 real-world topologies
key_result: Estimates end-to-end path delay on 106 unseen real topologies with about 3.8% MAPE across different queueing configurations.
limitation_or_critique: Digital twin is limited to transport-layer QoS metrics and assumes complete knowledge of the traffic matrix, which is rarely available in operational mobile networks.

title: DeepQueueNet: Towards Scalable and Generalized Network Performance Estimation with Packet-level Visibility
authors: Qingqing Yang; Xi Peng; Li Chen; Libin Liu; Jingze Zhang; Hong Xu; Baochun Li; Gong Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2022 Conference
summary: Hybrid simulator that keeps a queueing-theoretic skeleton and only replaces the intractable device-level parts with deep neural networks, preserving packet-level visibility.
method: Hybrid queueing theory + DNN learned simulator
data_or_testbed: Simulated networks of varied topologies and traffic management mechanisms; multi-GPU
key_result: Scales near-linearly with the number of GPUs and estimates average and 99th-percentile RTT more accurately than end-to-end DNN performance estimators.
limitation_or_critique: Requires sufficient per-device training data and targets switch-level queueing, leaving compute-bound virtualised network functions out of scope.

title: Predicting network performance using GNNs: generalization to larger unseen networks
authors: Miquel Farreras; Paola Soto; Miguel Camelo; Lluis Fabrega; Pere Vila
venue: NOMS 2022-2022 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Step-by-step modification of the RouteNet baseline, guided by networking concepts, to make GNN delay prediction generalise to networks much larger than those in training.
method: GNN (RouteNet variant) with feature engineering for scale generalisation
key_result: Reduces delay MAPE on larger unseen graphs from about 187% for the baseline to under 2%.
limitation_or_critique: Results are tied to a single challenge dataset of simulated networks, so generalisation beyond that distribution is not demonstrated.

title: MimicNet: Fast Performance Estimates for Data Center Networks with Machine Learning
authors: Qizhen Zhang; Kelvin K. W. Ng; Charles Kazer; Shen Yan; João Sedoc; Vincent Liu
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 ACM SIGCOMM 2021 Conference
summary: MimicNet simulates a small part of a data center at packet level and replaces the remaining clusters with learned models to obtain fast whole-network performance estimates.
method: Learned network simulator (ML surrogates of clusters)
data_or_testbed: Packet-level simulation of fat-tree data centers with thousands of servers
key_result: Achieves more than two orders of magnitude speed-up while keeping tail flow completion time, throughput and RTT estimates within 5% of full simulation.
limitation_or_critique: Relies on the symmetry of data-center topologies, so the approach does not transfer directly to heterogeneous, multi-domain mobile networks.

title: RouteNet: Leveraging Graph Neural Networks for Network Modeling and Optimization in SDN
authors: Krzysztof Rusek; Jose Suarez-Varela; Paul Almasan; Pere Barlet-Ros; Albert Cabellos-Aparicio
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
summary: Introduces RouteNet, a message-passing GNN over links and paths that predicts per source-destination delay, jitter and loss from topology, routing and traffic matrix.
method: Graph neural network (link-path message passing)
data_or_testbed: Packet-level simulation datasets (OMNeT++) on several topologies
key_result: Predicts mean delay, jitter and loss on unseen topologies, routings and traffic with a worst-case mean relative error of about 15%, and is used for routing optimisation and planning.
limitation_or_critique: Trained and tested on simulated wired SDN data with simple traffic models, so applicability to virtualised mobile core functions is not shown.

title: Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
authors: ITU-T
summary: Defines a logical architecture for integrating ML pipelines (sources, pre-processing, model, policy, sinks), an ML sandbox and an orchestrator into IMT-2020 networks.
method: Architectural framework
key_result: Introduces the ML sandbox concept for training and validating models before deployment, which anticipates digital-twin-based validation.
limitation_or_critique: Purely architectural and pre-dates 3GPP Rel-18 AI/ML management, so it gives no guidance on model accuracy, drift or safety guarantees.

title: IntAgent: NWDAF-Based Intent LLM Agent Towards Advanced Next Generation Networks
authors: Abdelrahman Soliman; Ahmed Refaey; Aiman Erbad; Amr Mohamed
venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Integrates an intent-fulfilling LLM agent with NWDAF by embedding an intent tools engine in the analytics engine and exposing scheduling, monitoring and analytics tools via an MCP server.
method: LLM agent with NWDAF analytics tools via Model Context Protocol
key_result: Demonstrates autonomous fulfilment of operator intents in ML-based traffic prediction and scheduled policy enforcement use cases.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation limited to two illustrative use cases; reliability, safety guards and latency of agentic decisions in the core are not quantified in the abstract.

title: Agent xG Core: Agentic AI for Next-Generation Mobile Core Network
authors: Maria Katarine Santana Barbosa; Kelvin Lopes Dias
summary: Adds an agentic AI-native layer over existing 3GPP core APIs in which a planner agent and an executor/critic agent run a closed loop to meet operator intents.
method: Multi-agent ReAct LLM system over 3GPP core APIs (MCP)
data_or_testbed: open-source core network with heterogeneous datasets; several LLMs
key_result: Shows an intent-driven, continuously adapting closed loop (e.g. load balancing) can be built on existing core APIs rather than new NFs.
limitation_or_critique: Prototype-level evaluation on an open-source core; behaviour under faults, hallucinations and scale is not established (preprint arXiv:2606.00417).

title: AICOM: A Novel LLM-based Autonomous Configuration Management in Cloud-Native 5GC
authors: Vitor Kussler Veronese; Zhiyi Zhang; Jean-François Maudoux; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi
summary: Proposes AICOM, combining deterministic automation, Kubernetes orchestration and GitOps with LLM agents to autonomously manage configuration of a cloud-native 5G core.
method: LLM agents in an intelligence layer separated from a GitOps automation layer
data_or_testbed: OpenAirInterface 5GC on Kubernetes; Gemini, Qwen and Llama models
key_result: Separating LLM understanding from deterministic execution enables autonomous configuration changes of 5GC NFs in an operator-led prototype.
limitation_or_critique: Operator-driven prototype whose quantitative results we could not inspect in full text; generality beyond one open-source core is unclear.

title: Intent-Based 5G Core Deployment Using Generative AI
authors: Dimitrios Brodimas; Nikolaos Tzanis; Alexios Birbas
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing, Networking and Communications (ICNC)
summary: Uses multimodal generative AI to translate textual and image-based intents into configuration files that deploy an open-source 5G core without human intervention.
method: Multimodal LLM intent-to-configuration translation
key_result: Demonstrates zero-touch deployment of a 5G core tailored to stakeholder intents from high-level descriptions.
limitation_or_critique: Addresses day-0 deployment only, not runtime assurance or closed-loop reconfiguration; extends the authors' EuCNC 2024 multimodal intent framework.

title: Intent-Based Management of Next-Generation Networks: an LLM-Centric Approach
authors: Abdelkader Mekrache; Adlen Ksentini; Christos Verikoukis
summary: Proposes an LLM-centric intent lifecycle architecture covering decomposition, translation, negotiation, activation and assurance of natural-language intents for network services.
method: LLM-based intent lifecycle management architecture
key_result: Real deployment shows natural-language intents being decomposed, translated and activated end to end on a 5G platform.
limitation_or_critique: Validation is a functional demonstration with limited quantitative assurance results; builds on the authors' NetSoft 2024 intent-to-NSD translation work.

title: Semantic Routing for Enhanced Performance of LLM-Assisted Intent-Based 5G Core Network Management and Orchestration
authors: Dimitrios Michael Manias; Ali Chouman; Abdallah Shami
summary: Adds a semantic router in front of an LLM to classify operator intents for 5G core management and orchestration, with an intent dataset and study of encoders and quantisation.
method: Semantic routing plus LLM intent extraction pipeline
data_or_testbed: custom dataset of 5G core user intents
key_result: Semantic routing improved accuracy and efficiency compared with stand-alone prompted LLMs.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on intent extraction/classification only, without closing the loop to actual NF reconfiguration; follows the same group's DRCN 2024 LLM intent-extraction paper.

title: AI-driven Closed-loop Automation in 5G and beyond Mobile Networks
authors: Raouf Boutaba; Nashid Shahriar; Mohammad A. Salahuddin; Shihabur R. Chowdhury; Niloy Saha; Alexander James
venue: Proceedings of the 4th FlexNets Workshop on Flexible Networks Artificial Intelligence Supported Network Flexibility and Agility
summary: Vision paper extending the MAPE control loop for closed-loop service orchestration and network management in 5G and beyond, discussing the role of AI/ML in each stage.
method: Position paper; extended MAPE closed-loop architecture
key_result: Frames closed-loop automation as necessary for strict differentiated QoS and lists open research challenges for AI-driven loops.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop vision paper (ACM FlexNets) without implementation or evaluation; later works from the same group provide the concrete NWDAF-based realisation.

title: Management and orchestration; Intent driven management services for mobile networks
authors: 3GPP
summary: Defines intent-driven management services for mobile networks, including intent expectations, intent-driven closed loops, negotiation, feasibility checks and intent reports.
method: Standard specification (Stage 2/3 intent management)
key_result: Provides an intent information model and RESTful solution set with use cases spanning RAN, 5GC, edge and energy saving, with Rel-19 and draft Rel-20 versions extending it.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies interfaces and models but not how intents are translated or assured, which is where most LLM-based research operates without conformance to this model.

title: From Agentic to Autogenic Network Management for AI-Native 6G and Beyond: A Standards Perspective
authors: Petar Djukic; Sudipta Acharya; Takai Eddine Kennouche; Burak Kantarci
summary: Proposes autogenic network management that extends agentic management with self-programming, self-reflection and self-architecting, aligned with TM Forum, 3GPP and ETSI directions.
method: Reference architecture with staged deployment and standards analysis
data_or_testbed: TM Forum autonomous network use-case scenarios
key_result: Outlines a staged path from human-supervised large-AI-model agents towards autonomous operation and a research roadmap.
limitation_or_critique: Conceptual architecture without experimental validation; the self-programming premise raises verification and safety questions it does not resolve.
standards_link: TM Forum AN; 3GPP TS 28.100; ETSI ZSM

title: AGILE-6G: Agentic AI for Autonomous Management of 6G Network/Application Services
authors: Angelos Antonopoulos; Elli Kartsakli; Nikolaos Bartzoudis; Dimitrios Brodimas; Dejan Vukobratovic; Dimitris Tsolkas; Ferran Diego; George Roumelas; Lechosław Tomaszewski
summary: Introduces Domain Agentic Systems and the AGILE-6G framework that places an agentic intelligence layer above existing management systems across end-to-end and per-domain scopes.
method: Agentic orchestration architecture with use-case illustration
key_result: Shows how collaborating agents can automatically reconfigure network and application services for self-healing and adaptive management.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style blueprint with qualitative use cases; no quantitative evaluation or explicit mapping to 3GPP core NFs.

title: Management and orchestration; Levels of autonomous network
authors: 3GPP
summary: Specifies concepts of autonomous networks and autonomous network levels together with use cases and requirements for evaluating the autonomy of 3GPP network management workflows.
method: Standard specification (autonomy levels framework)
key_result: Gives a standardised scale against which closed-loop and agentic management solutions can be positioned, aligned with the TM Forum level concept.
limitation_or_critique: Level definitions are qualitative and per-workflow; academic papers rarely evaluate their systems against these levels, limiting comparability.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Closed-Control Loops for Beyond 5G Multi-Domain Zero-Touch Networks
authors: Nathan Franklin Saraiva de Sousa; Md Tariqul Islam; Raza Ul Mustafa; Danny Alex Lachos Perez; Christian Esteve Rothenberg; Pedro Henrique Gomes
venue: Journal of Network and Systems Management
summary: Proposes a multi-domain ZSM architecture where per-domain ML-assisted closed control loops collaborate for end-to-end service healing, demonstrated on video streaming.
method: ZSM-based multi-domain closed loops with ML for SLA violation estimation and root cause
data_or_testbed: emulation with real mobile network traces
key_result: ML helps estimate QoS-to-QoE at the edge and link service degradation to faulty transport links, enabling cooperative healing.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated in emulation on one DASH use case with transport-network faults rather than 5G core NFs; journal extension of the CLARA framework (NFV-SDN 2021).

title: Zero-touch network and Service Management (ZSM); Closed-Loop Automation; Part 1: Enablers
authors: ETSI ZSM
summary: Specifies the enablers for closed-loop automation in the ZSM framework, including closed-loop governance, coordination, delegation and escalation between loops.
method: Standard specification (closed-loop enablers)
key_result: Defines services to create, run and supervise closed loops and to coordinate hierarchies of loops across management domains, building on the ZSM 002 reference architecture.
limitation_or_critique: Framework-level and implementation-agnostic, it leaves loop conflict resolution and AI model trust largely to implementers and is not tied to 3GPP core NFs.
standards_link: ETSI GS ZSM 002; ETSI GS ZSM 009-2

title: Intent-driven Closed Loops for Autonomous Networks
authors: Pedro Henrique Gomes; Magnus Buhrgard; János Harmatos; Swarup Kumar Mohalik; Dinand Roeland; Jörg Niemöller
summary: Proposes using intents to coordinate hierarchies of ZSM closed loops across autonomous management domains via delegation and escalation.
method: Intent-driven methodology for hierarchical closed-loop coordination
key_result: Shows how setting non-conflicting goals per loop through intents can extend ZSM to coordinate multiple intent-driven closed loops.
limitation_or_critique: Illustrated with a single slicing assurance example rather than a quantitative evaluation, and authored by an industrial group pushing a specific design.
standards_link: ETSI ZSM 009-1; TM Forum intent; 3GPP TS 28.312

title: Intent-Based Networking - Concepts and Definitions
authors: IRTF NMRG
summary: IRTF NMRG informational RFC clarifying the notion of intent, distinguishing it from policy, and outlining the functions and lifecycle of intent-based networking.
method: Informational RFC (concepts and terminology)
key_result: Establishes shared terminology and an intent lifecycle with fulfilment and assurance loops that later IBN work commonly cites.
limitation_or_critique: Conceptual IP-network oriented reference with no mobile-core specifics or evaluation; it is background rather than a technical solution.

title: 5GC-Trace-RCA: Distributed Tracing-Based Root Cause Analysis for QoS Troubleshooting in Cloud Native 5G Core Network
authors: Anping Zhao; Frederic Desnoes; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Proposes an end-to-end RCA architecture that builds anomaly propagation chains from causal relations in distributed traces of cloud-native 5G core procedures.
method: Distributed tracing + causal anomaly propagation chains
data_or_testbed: Real 5G traffic from a macro-cell at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airport
key_result: Localises diverse service failures and performance degradations across 5GC NFs and improves root-cause precision by exposing cascading effects.
limitation_or_critique: One of very few RCA works on real 5GC traffic, but tracing instrumentation of the core is assumed and generality beyond the studied deployment is not shown.

title: MDAF-Based Explainable Failure Prediction for Network Functions in 5G/6G
authors: Sukhyun Nam; Wonseok Choi; James Won-Ki Hong
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Implements a 3GPP-style Management Data Analytics Function that predicts and explains NF failures using multi-domain metrics and logs, a CNV-GRU time-series predictor, SHAP attributions and LLM explanations.
method: CNV-GRU with focal loss + SHAP + LLM natural-language reasoning
key_result: Reaches up to 78.6% F1 for detection, 73.0% for 3-minute-ahead prediction and 77.8% accuracy in naming the responsible NF.
limitation_or_critique: Rare explicit MDAF implementation, but accuracy levels remain modest and evaluation is limited to one open-source testbed.

title: Deep Learning-Based Proactive Anomaly Detection for 5G Core Control Plane Network Function Interactions
authors: Yawen Tan; Jiajia Liu; Yuanhao Li; Jiadai Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
summary: Proposes 5GCGuard, a deep sequence model that learns normal NF-to-NF service interaction patterns in the SBA control plane and flags deviations as anomalies.
method: Attention-based sequence model with multi-task learning, probabilistic labelling and automatic thresholding
key_result: Outperforms comparison schemes on the testbed and, in case studies, proactively detects several kinds of abnormal NF interactions.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on a single self-built testbed with injected attack scenarios, so transfer to multi-vendor operational cores is unproven and root-cause localisation is not addressed.

title: Granomaly: A Framework for Anomaly Detection in 5G Core Network Control Plane Traffic with Temporal Graph Neural Networks
authors: Tobias Fritz; Alexander Schwankner; Jan-Hendrik Wissing; Robin Buchta; Gabi Dreo Rodosek
venue: NOMS 2025-2025 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Represents 5G core control-plane traffic as a temporal graph and applies temporal graph neural networks to detect subtle anomalies, positioning the approach alongside NWDAF analytics.
method: Temporal graph neural networks (two TGNN variants)
data_or_testbed: Simulated 5G core; two benchmark datasets released
key_result: Shows that TGNNs detect subtle control-plane traffic anomalies and contributes two TGNN-ready benchmark datasets.
limitation_or_critique: Relies on a simulated core and security-style anomalies, and leaves integration with a real NWDAF and root-cause localisation open.

title: Modality-Agnostic Root Cause Analysis with Optimal Transport for 5G Core Network
authors: Nobukazu Fukuda; Haruhisa Nozue; Kenichi Tayama
summary: Proposes an unsupervised, entity-centric RCA method for 5G core failures that compares telemetry distributions with optimal transport, so it works when some data modalities are missing.
method: Optimal transport on heterogeneous telemetry (metrics, logs, packets) keyed to entities
data_or_testbed: 5G core connected to an IP backbone (operator lab)
key_result: Improves RCA accuracy over baselines under both complete and partial observability.
limitation_or_critique: Lab-scale evaluation by a single operator group; no comparison with standardised analytics outputs such as NWDAF or MDA reports.

title: 5G Core Fault Detection and Root Cause Analysis using Machine Learning and Generative AI
authors: Joseph H. R. Isaac; Harish Saradagam; Nallamothu Pardhasaradhi
summary: Describes a fault-analysis engine that classifies faulty frames in 5G packet-core PCAP and log test files with NLP models and uses an LLM grounded in 3GPP and product documents to suggest fixes.
method: NLP classifiers on PCAP frames + document-grounded LLM for remediation hints
key_result: Reports high frame-classification accuracy with an 80-20 split and LLM-generated domain explanations of errors.
limitation_or_critique: Preprint (accepted at a small conference) targeting test-lab artefacts rather than live operations; LLM explanation quality is not rigorously evaluated.

title: Fault Diagnosis Using Hybrid Transfer Learning for VNF-based 5G Core Networks
authors: Tianhao Zhu; Yoshiaki Narusue; Hiroyuki Morikawa
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Network Function Virtualization and Software Defined Networks (NFV-SDN)
summary: Combines model-, instance- and feature-based transfer learning to move fault-diagnosis knowledge from a scale-out 5G testbed to a real 5G core with little labelled data.
method: Hybrid transfer learning for fault classification across VNFs
key_result: Hybrid transfer learning beats no-transfer and plain model-based transfer, with 70% of fault labels reaching F1 above 0.9.
limitation_or_critique: Addresses the important data-scarcity problem, but the target network is small and the fault taxonomy is limited to predefined classes.

title: A Method of Alarm Correlation and Root Cause Analysis in 5G Core Network
authors: Shiyu Zhou; Xiqing Liu; Xinzhou Cheng; Zhenqiao Zhao; Jingyun Wang; Tian Xiao
summary: Proposes alarm correlation and root-cause analysis for an operator 5G core by combining an expert-built rule base with graph neural networks.
method: Expert rules + GNN-based alarm correlation
key_result: Authors claim substantial gains in operation and maintenance efficiency; detailed quantitative results were not visible to us.
limitation_or_critique: Short proceedings chapter whose full evaluation could not be checked; rule-base dependence limits portability across vendors.

title: ADSeq-5GCN: Anomaly Detection from Network Traffic Sequences in 5G Core Network Control Plane
authors: Zixu Tian; Rajendra Patil; Mohan Gurusamy; Joshua McCloud
venue: 2023 IEEE 24th International Conference on High Performance Switching and Routing (HPSR)
summary: Models captured 5G core control-plane traffic as sequences of service events and uses a Bi-LSTM to predict the next event, treating mispredictions as anomalies.
method: Bi-LSTM next-event prediction on NF-to-NF traffic
key_result: Reports clearly better detection than baseline models across several attack and misbehaviour scenarios on the free5GC testbed.
limitation_or_critique: Testbed-scale evaluation centred on hostile-NF scenarios; it detects but does not localise or explain faults.

title: Deep Learning-Based Log Anomaly Detection for 5G Core Network
authors: Yawen Tan; Jiadai Wang; Jiajia Liu; Yuanhao Li
venue: 2023 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC)
summary: Builds a modular deep-learning log anomaly detection pipeline (parsing, grouping, feature extraction, training) for internal failures of a virtualised 5G core.
method: Log parsing + deep learning classifiers
data_or_testbed: Cloud-native 5G testbed with injected anomalies (own log dataset)
key_result: Best configuration exceeds 97% F1 on the collected 5G core log dataset.
limitation_or_critique: Log dataset comes from one open-source core implementation with synthetic fault injection, and the work stops at detection without root-cause attribution.

title: Graph-based Interpretable Anomaly Detection Framework for Network Slice Management in Beyond 5G Networks
authors: Ashima Chawla; Anne-Marie Bosneag; Anestis Dalgkitsis
venue: NOMS 2023-2023 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Presents G5IAD, which models correlations among multivariate network-slice KPIs with graph convolutions and GRU forecasting to detect and explain slice-level anomalies.
method: GCN + GRU forecasting + probabilistic anomaly classification
key_result: Provides unsupervised, interpretable slice-level anomaly detection intended to speed up root-cause analysis for self-managed slices.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-based evaluation; explanation is at KPI-feature level rather than identification of the faulty NF.

title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
authors: Hao Zhou; Mandar Kulkarni; Hao Chen; Yan Xin; Charlie Jianzhong Zhang
summary: Reviews the evolution of telecom RCA toward LLM-enabled techniques and proposes a structured, evidence-grounded reasoning framework to curb hallucination in LLM diagnosis.
method: Canonical telemetry contexts + enforced decision-path reasoning with LLMs
key_result: Improves diagnostic accuracy and decision consistency over baseline LLM techniques on both datasets.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style article; the datasets are mainly radio-performance troubleshooting rather than core NF faults.

title: Root Cause Analysis for Microservice System based on Causal Inference: How Far Are We?
authors: Luan Pham; Huong Ha; Hongyu Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 39th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
summary: Benchmarks nine causal-discovery and twenty-one causal-inference RCA methods for microservices on synthetic and real-system datasets.
method: Large-scale empirical comparison
data_or_testbed: Synthetic datasets and benchmark microservice systems
key_result: Finds that no method dominates and that results on synthetic data poorly predict performance on real systems.
limitation_or_critique: Valuable reality check, but restricted to IT microservices; telecom-specific fault propagation through 3GPP procedures is untested.

title: Automatic Root Cause Analysis via Large Language Models for Cloud Incidents
authors: Yinfang Chen; Huaibing Xie; Minghua Ma; Yu Kang; Xin Gao; Liu Shi; Yunjie Cao; Xuedong Gao; Hao Fan; Ming Wen; Jun Zeng; Supriyo Ghosh; Xuchao Zhang; Chaoyun Zhang; Qingwei Lin; Saravan Rajmohan; Dongmei Zhang; Tianyin Xu
venue: Proceedings of the Nineteenth European Conference on Computer Systems
summary: Presents RCACopilot, an LLM-powered on-call system that routes incidents to handlers, gathers diagnostic data, predicts root-cause categories and writes explanations.
method: Incident handlers + LLM root-cause category prediction and explanation
data_or_testbed: One year of Microsoft production incidents
key_result: Reaches RCA accuracy up to 0.766 on real incidents, and its data-collection component has been in production for years.
limitation_or_critique: Proprietary data and cloud-service incident types; requires curated handlers, so porting to telecom operations would need domain workflows.

title: RCAgent: Cloud Root Cause Analysis by Autonomous Agents with Tool-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Zefan Wang; Zichuan Liu; Yingying Zhang; Aoxiao Zhong; Jihong Wang; Fengbin Yin; Lunting Fan; Lingfei Wu; Qingsong Wen
venue: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
summary: Proposes a tool-augmented autonomous LLM agent for privacy-aware industrial RCA that collects data and analyses it freely, with trajectory-level self-consistency and context management.
method: ReAct-style tool-using LLM agent with self-consistency over action trajectories
key_result: Consistently outperforms ReAct on root cause, solution, evidence and responsibility prediction, and is deployed in production diagnosis.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on one cloud platform with internal models; safety of agent actions in a live network is not studied.

title: Eadro: An End-to-End Troubleshooting Framework for Microservices on Multi-source Data
authors: Cheryl Lee; Tianyi Yang; Zhuangbin Chen; Yuxin Su; Michael R. Lyu
venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
summary: Jointly learns anomaly detection and root-cause localisation from traces, logs and KPIs by modelling intra-service behaviour and inter-service dependencies.
method: Multi-modal deep learning with graph modelling of service dependencies
data_or_testbed: Microservice benchmark systems with fault injection
key_result: Shows that coupling detection and localisation on multi-source data outperforms single-source, two-stage pipelines.
limitation_or_critique: Supervised and trained on benchmark applications; label availability in operator networks is a practical obstacle.

title: Digital-Twin assisted Root Cause Analysis of Anomalies in NFV Environment
authors: Weili Wang; Qianbin Chen; Tong Liu; Lun Tang
venue: ICC 2021 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Uses a digital twin to maintain a real-time anomaly-fault dependency matrix in NFV and solves root-cause localisation as a dynamic set-covering problem with parallel hidden Markov models.
method: Digital twin + HMM-based dynamic set covering solved with ADMM
key_result: Simulations show the distributed digital-twin assisted RCA identifies minimal faulty-component sets better than compared methods.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on VM/server faults rather than 5G core NF procedures.

title: MicroRCA: Root Cause Localization of Performance Issues in Microservices
authors: Li Wu; Johan Tordsson; Erik Elmroth; Odej Kao
venue: NOMS 2020 - 2020 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Locates root causes of microservice performance issues by building an attributed graph linking services and hosts and ranking candidates via anomaly propagation, without application instrumentation.
method: Attributed graph + personalised PageRank-style propagation
data_or_testbed: Microservice benchmark on Kubernetes with injected faults
key_result: Reports 89% precision and 97% mean average precision, ahead of earlier methods.
limitation_or_critique: Widely used baseline, but limited to metric data and a single benchmark application; telecom NFs are not evaluated.

title: Safe RL for Core Network autoscaling
authors: Xinqi Long; Guillaume Fraysse
venue: 2024 20th International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Formulates core-network autoscaling as a constrained (safe) RL problem so that exploration avoids unsafe scaling actions during training.
method: Safe reinforcement learning with constraint design and tuning
data_or_testbed: Gym-based simulator and Magma open-source core
key_result: Safe RL agents behaved more safely during exploration than unconstrained RL, improving prospects for real-world deployment.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference paper with limited workloads; safety is defined on resource/QoS constraints only and not tied to 3GPP overload control.

title: Autoscaling Packet Core Network Functions with Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jatinder Singh; Shantanu Verma; Yoichi Matsuo; Francesca Fossati; Guillaume Fraysse
venue: NOMS 2023-2023 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Applies a dueling double deep Q-network to proactively scale cloud resources of packet-core NFs, comparing it with threshold-based autoscaling on a Magma core testbed.
method: Deep RL (D3QN) with reward combining resource usage and workload
key_result: DRL scaling cut dropped sessions by up to two orders of magnitude versus threshold scaling while keeping resource usage within bounds.
limitation_or_critique: Single-NF scaling on a Magma (4G/5G hybrid) core; no coordination with NRF/SCP-based selection or multi-NF dependencies.

title: A Reliable AMF Scaling and Load Balancing Framework for 5G Core Networks
authors: Ali Chouman; Dimitrios Michael Manias; Abdallah Shami
venue: 2023 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
summary: Optimisation framework that computes the minimum number of AMF instances from traffic-class distributions and assigns relative capacities for load balancing within an AMF set.
method: Optimisation-based scaling with weighted load balancing
key_result: Resilience level is tunable through the problem formulation and the balancer spreads load evenly across AMF instances.
limitation_or_critique: Demand is assumed known/projected rather than learned online, and evaluation is on a small emulated prototype.

title: Dynamic Network Slice Scaling Assisted by Attention-Based Prediction in 5G Core Network
authors: Chien-Nguyen Nhu; Minho Park
summary: Uses an attention-based encoder-decoder for multivariate forecasting of VNF resource usage to scale 5GC network slices proactively, balancing SLA violations against over-provisioning.
method: Attention-based seq2seq forecasting plus proactive scaling policy
key_result: Attention-based prediction improved short- and long-term accuracy and reduced combined SLA-violation and over-provisioning cost versus reactive and baseline proactive scaling.
limitation_or_critique: Scaling is slice/VNF-resource oriented and does not consider SBA-level request routing or NF instance selection after scale-out.

title: Cloud Native 5G: an Efficient Orchestration of Cloud Native 5G System
authors: Abderaouf Khichane; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi; Mourad Gueroui
venue: NOMS 2022-2022 IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Proposes an orchestration framework for 5G cloud-native NFs that jointly provisions IT and network resources and automates lifecycle management, validated on an auto-scaling use case.
method: CNF orchestration framework (Kubernetes-based) with auto-scaling
key_result: Reported good deployment and upgrade times, low packet loss and balanced resource allocation in experiments.
limitation_or_critique: Scaling logic is rule-based rather than learned, and comparison baselines are limited.

title: AI-Based Resource Management in Beyond 5G Cloud Native Environment
authors: Abderrahmane Boudi; Miloud Bagaa; Petteri Poyhonen; Tarik Taleb; Hannu Flinck
summary: Magazine article proposing a hierarchical closed-loop, AI-based framework for managing resources of cloud-native B5G network functions, aligned with ETSI ZSM, plus a cloud-native simulator.
method: Hierarchical closed-loop ML management framework; cloud-native simulator
data_or_testbed: Custom cloud-native simulator validated against testbed metrics
key_result: Shows the simulator reproduces real testbed behaviour on several metrics, enabling fast evaluation of AI-based CNF management policies.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation centres on simulator fidelity rather than on concrete NF scaling or selection decisions in a standard 5GC.

title: Scaling UPF Instances in 5G/6G Core With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Hai T. Nguyen; Tien Van Do; Csaba Rotter
summary: Applies PPO-based deep RL with a threshold-shaped reward to scale containerised UPF instances on Kubernetes according to PDU-session demand, with an SVM guard against unwanted actions.
method: Deep RL (PPO) plus SVM action filter
key_result: DRL saved about 2.7-3.8% of pods on average compared with Kubernetes HPA, and the SVM variant up to 4.5%.
limitation_or_critique: User-plane focus with modest gains and simulation-based evaluation; SMF-driven UPF selection is not jointly optimised.

title: Cognitive Service Architecture for 6G Core Network
authors: Yuanzhe Li; Jie Huang; Qibo Sun; Tao Sun; Shangguang Wang
summary: Conceptualises a cognitive, bio-inspired (octopus nervous system) service architecture for the 6G core in which distributed intelligence augments the SBA.
method: Architecture proposal with case study
key_result: A case study suggests that distributed cognitive services can improve QoS handling relative to a conventional SBA core.
limitation_or_critique: Visionary design with limited quantitative validation and no mapping to 3GPP NRF/SCP procedures.

title: Open-Source 5G Core Platforms: A Low-Cost Solution and Performance Evaluation
authors: Maria Barbosa; Marcelo Silva; Ednelson Cavalcanti; Kelvin Dias
summary: Reviews major open-source 5GC platforms and compares their control- and user-plane performance on a COTS 5G SA testbed.
method: Comparative review and experimental evaluation
data_or_testbed: Open5GS, OAI, free5GC on COTS SA testbed
key_result: Open5GS gave the lowest control-plane latencies, OAI the highest data rates and free5GC the lowest resource consumption.
limitation_or_critique: Small-scale single-node testbed; results are sensitive to versions and configuration and do not cover scaling behaviour.

title: Performance and Viability Analysis of Deploying Cloud-native 5G Autoscaling Platforms
authors: Amber Yucebas; Ruoting Xiong; Yi Ren; Xu Zhang; Gerard Parr
venue: Proceedings of the 1st free5GC World Forum 2025
summary: Compares two stateless 5GC autoscaling platforms, CoreKube and free5GC-helm, under high synthetic load on a public cloud.
method: Experimental comparison with PacketRusher load generation
data_or_testbed: CoreKube and free5GC-helm on Hetzner Cloud; PacketRusher
key_result: free5GC-helm autoscaling hit bottlenecks early, mainly because of decisions made in the NRF.
limitation_or_critique: Short workshop-style paper (4 pages) at a new venue; analysis limited to two platforms and reactive autoscaling.

title: Control Plane Performance Benchmarking and Feature Analysis of Popular Open-Source 5G Core Networks: OpenAirInterface, Open5GS, and free5GC
authors: Tariro Mukute; Lusani Mamushiane; Albert A. Lysko; Elena-Ramona Modroiu; Thomas Magedanz; Joyce Mwangama
summary: Maps NF operations to 5G procedures and benchmarks the control planes of OAI, Open5GS and free5GC with macro- (procedure time) and micro- (system-call) benchmarking.
method: Macro/micro benchmarking with UE registration traffic generator
data_or_testbed: OAI, Open5GS, free5GC; custom traffic generator; released artefacts
key_result: Macro-level procedure performance correlates with micro-level system-call behaviour, which the authors use to pinpoint architectural improvements per core.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on registration-type procedures on single deployments; autoscaling and multi-instance NF selection are outside scope.

title: Evaluating 5G Core Service Mesh Encapsulations in Cloud Deployments
authors: Tolga O. Atalay; Alireza Famili; Angelos Stavrou
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Network Function Virtualization and Software Defined Networks (NFV-SDN)
summary: Introduces 5G-NECTAR, a framework that wraps 5GC NFs in a custom sidecar-based service mesh with OpenTelemetry/Jaeger tracing to measure overhead in public-cloud deployments across HTTP versions.
method: Service-mesh encapsulation and distributed tracing measurement framework
data_or_testbed: 5G core on AWS with sidecar proxies, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger
key_result: Quantifies the control-plane overhead and cost of service-mesh encapsulation for cloud-hosted 5GC and provides operational lessons for MVNOs.
limitation_or_critique: Measurement study without adaptive or learned routing/selection policies in the mesh.

title: Investigating Inter-NF Dependencies in Cloud-Native 5G Core Networks
authors: Endri Goshi; Michael Jarschel; Rastin Pries; Mu He; Wolfgang Kellerer
venue: 2021 17th International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Studies how inter-NF dependencies in a Kubernetes-orchestrated free5GC affect resource utilisation during control-plane procedures, using a custom gNB/UE emulator.
method: Experimental characterisation of NF resource coupling
data_or_testbed: free5GC on Kubernetes; custom gNB/UE emulator
key_result: Shows that ignoring inter-NF dependencies leads to inefficient scaling where a single NF can bottleneck the whole core.
limitation_or_critique: Descriptive study on one open-source core; it motivates but does not propose a dependency-aware scaling or selection algorithm.

title: Next generation of microservices for the 5G Service‐Based Architecture
authors: João Bourbon Moreira; Henrique Mamede; Vasco Pereira; Bruno Sousa
summary: Evaluates VM-based versus container/serverless deployment of SBA network functions and compares HTTP versions, including HTTP/3 over QUIC, for the service-based interfaces.
method: Experimental comparison of deployment models and HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3
data_or_testbed: Kubernetes microservice testbed with emulated loss/delay
key_result: HTTP/3 brought performance benefits under lossy or delayed links, though connection tracking must be engineered for high request volumes.
limitation_or_critique: Synthetic NF services rather than a full 5GC; 3GPP still mandates HTTP/2 over TCP, limiting immediate applicability.

title: System architecture for the 5G System (5GS)
authors: 3GPP
summary: Stage-2 architecture of the 5GS defining the SBA, NF services, NRF-based discovery, SCP indirect communication models and NF/NF-set selection principles.
method: Standard (Stage 2)
key_result: Defines direct and indirect (SCP, delegated discovery) communication options and NF set/load-based selection inputs that research on NF selection must respect.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies selection inputs and frameworks but leaves selection and load-balancing algorithms to implementation.

title: 5G System; Technical Realization of Service Based Architecture; Stage 3
authors: 3GPP
summary: Stage-3 realisation of the SBA: HTTP/2-based SBI protocol stack, indirect communication via SCP, load and overload control, and error handling.
method: Standard (Stage 3)
key_result: Specifies load-control and overload-control information exchange between NFs and SCP, the hooks for adaptive load balancing.
limitation_or_critique: Overload/load control is signalled but policies are left open, which is where AI-based approaches could plug in.

title: 5G System; Network function repository services; Stage 3
authors: 3GPP
summary: Stage-3 specification of NRF services (NF registration, status subscription, discovery, access token) and NF profile attributes used for selection.
method: Standard (Stage 3)
key_result: Defines NF profile fields such as load, capacity, priority and locality that drive discovery responses and consumer-side selection.
limitation_or_critique: Load information in NF profiles is coarse and update-rate limited, motivating analytics-assisted selection.

title: Profitable Energy-Efficient UPF and Application Placement and Routing in Dynamic 5G Edge
authors: Endri Goshi; Ece Nur Şen; Hasanin Harkous; Shohreh Ahvar; Rastin Pries; Fidan Mehmeti; Wolfgang Kellerer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
summary: Jointly places UPFs and edge applications and routes demand in a multi-owner edge, maximising operator profit while minimising energy and migration overhead.
method: multi-objective optimisation + ranked greedy heuristic
key_result: The heuristic balances profit, energy and migrations better than baseline strategies in dynamic edge scenarios.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only; energy model is analytical and the approach is not tied to 3GPP management or analytics interfaces.

title: Energy-Efficient Placement of Logical Functionalities in 5G Networks
authors: Junior Momo Ziazet; Brigitte Jaumard
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Jointly places DUs, CUs and UPFs with traffic routing in a cloud-RAN/edge setting to minimise energy subject to latency and QoS, using column generation and a heuristic.
method: ILP + column generation + heuristic
key_result: Reduces energy by up to 14% with near-optimal solutions and shows that static peak-time placement wastes energy over the day.
limitation_or_critique: Optimisation is offline per time period; the control-plane core NFs and runtime re-placement costs are outside scope; extends the FNWF 2023 conference paper.

title: Management and orchestration; Energy efficiency of 5G
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA5 specification of energy-efficiency KPIs (5GC EE based on N3 data volume, per-slice-type EE), energy-saving use cases such as edge-UPF switch-off, VNF/VNFC energy estimation and energy-related information models.
method: standard (management stage 1-3)
key_result: Defines the normative EE metrics and centralised/distributed energy-saving solutions that core-network optimisation work should report against.
limitation_or_critique: Core EE is reduced to user-plane data volume per joule; control-plane NF energy and AI-driven core energy saving remain largely unspecified.

title: AGORA: Agentic Green Orchestration Architecture for Beyond 5G Networks
authors: Rodrigo Moreira; Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira; Maycon Leone Maciel Peixoto; Flávio De Oliveira Silva
summary: Embeds a local tool-augmented LLM agent in the mobile-network control loop that turns natural-language sustainability goals into telemetry-grounded actions on the UPF for energy-aware traffic steering.
method: tool-augmented LLM agent (intent-driven closed loop)
key_result: Finds strong latency-energy coupling in tool-driven loops and shows compact LLMs can execute the policies correctly with a low energy footprint, including migration under stressed MEC.
limitation_or_critique: Prototype-scale evaluation of a single actuation point (UPF steering); no alignment with 3GPP intent (TS 28.312) or energy KPIs (TS 28.310), and safety of LLM actions is not formally bounded.

title: Dynamic AI-Based UPF Switching: Adapting for Performance/Energy-Efficiency in 5G Networks
authors: Sokratis Christakis; Nikos Makris; Serge Fdida; Thanasis Korakis
summary: Proactively switches between two software UPF implementations (SPGW-U and VPP) using an LSTM throughput predictor to trade throughput against energy.
method: LSTM prediction + switching policy
data_or_testbed: testbed with SPGW-U and VPP-based UPFs
key_result: Shows that the higher-throughput VPP UPF costs much more energy, so predictive switching can save energy while meeting throughput.
limitation_or_critique: Only two UPF implementations; session continuity during switching and multi-NF effects are not addressed.

title: A measurement-based approach to analyze the power consumption of the softwarized 5G core
authors: Arturo Bellin; Fabrizio Granelli; Daniele Munaretto
summary: Proposes and validates a measurement methodology for the power draw of a virtualised 5G core on an edge node, comparing bare metal, containers and VMs and several open-source cores.
method: testbed measurement with hardware and software power meters
data_or_testbed: COTS server; open-source 5G cores; bare metal/containers/VMs
key_result: Shows that virtualisation framework and 5GC software choice significantly change power consumption and that real-time power monitoring is feasible.
limitation_or_critique: Single edge node and emulated traffic; no per-NF power model generalisable to carrier-grade deployments; extends the authors' NetSoft 2023 preliminary study.

title: Power Consumption-Aware 5G Edge UPF Selection using Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Arturo Bellin; Nicola Di Cicco; Daniele Munaretto; Fabrizio Granelli
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Network Function Virtualization and Software Defined Networks (NFV-SDN)
summary: A DRL agent selects among distributed edge/cloud UPF instances at session set-up using real-time host power measurements plus user latency and bandwidth needs.
method: deep reinforcement learning
data_or_testbed: edge-cloud 5GC setup with measured host power
key_result: Beats heuristic UPF selection with lower power and fewer latency violations, and shows measured power is a better input than CPU utilisation.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on a small deployment; integration with SMF UPF-selection procedures and NWDAF/PCF signalling is not specified.

title: DeMPUP: Energy-Efficient UPF Placement for Beyond 5G Social Metaverse Traffic
authors: Nairit Das; Kounteya Sarkar; Tushar Bose; Aneek Adhya; Sudip Misra
summary: Formulates a core-network power model and a non-linear program jointly selecting the gNB-to-edge path and the UPF host that minimise power, decomposed for scalability.
method: NLP optimisation + decomposition heuristic
key_result: The decomposed algorithm runs in linear time in the number of nodes while significantly reducing power versus baselines.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only with a static power model; no AI/learning and no validation on a real 5GC.

title: Study on Energy Efficiency and Energy Saving
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA2 Rel-19 study on 5GS enhancements for energy efficiency and saving: energy-related information collection and exposure, NWDAF energy analytics, and policy/subscription control using energy as a service criterion.
method: standard (architecture study)
key_result: Selects solutions for NF energy information collection and exposure that feed the Rel-19 EnergySys normative work in TS 23.501/23.502/23.503.
limitation_or_critique: Study report; reportedly scoped out part of the subscription/policy service-criteria key issue, and leaves energy-aware NF selection algorithms to implementations.

title: Enabling Energy-Efficient Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler
authors: Riccardo Miracapillo; Stefano Galantino; Attilio Oliva; Fulvio Risso
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Presents DREEM, a Kubernetes autoscaler for bare-metal clusters that chooses which servers to power off to save energy while preserving performance.
method: server-selection optimisation in Kubernetes autoscaler
key_result: Reduces the average number of active nodes and energy use without degrading responsiveness.
limitation_or_critique: Generic cloud workloads; transfer to stateful 5GC CNFs with session state and HA constraints is untested.

title: Power prediction and energy aware placement of containers over virtual machines
authors: Rafael Albuquerque; Brigitte Jaumard
summary: Trains ML models on physical-server power-sensor data to predict power and drive energy-aware container placement under realistic 5G traffic.
method: ML regression (XGBoost) + placement
key_result: XGBoost reaches R2 of 91.2% and placement cuts energy by about 3% without explicit consolidation.
limitation_or_critique: Modest energy gain and container workloads are not mapped to specific 5GC NFs.

title: Estimation of 5G Core Power Consumption for Open RAN Deployments
authors: Jean Z. Correia; Fuad M. Abinader; Ivan Aldaya
venue: 2025 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
summary: Measures the power of an O-RAN-based 5G core testbed under varying numbers of UEs and offered throughput and fits a predictive model.
method: testbed measurement + linear regression
data_or_testbed: small O-RAN testbed with up to 8 emulated UEs
key_result: Finds throughput, not user count, drives core power in the tested range, and a simple linear model predicts power accurately.
limitation_or_critique: Very small scale (8 UEs) in a workshop venue; linearity may not hold for control-plane-heavy or large deployments.

title: Real-Time Energy Consumption and Carbon Footprint Estimation of AI Agents in 6G
authors: Lucas Otávio Nascimento De Araújo; Abdelkader Outtagarts
summary: Demonstrates real-time estimation of energy and carbon footprint during training and inference of a DRL agent for mMTC admission control.
method: energy/carbon instrumentation of DRL
key_result: Maps the energy-delay efficiency landscape of training versus inference for the DRL agent across scenarios.
limitation_or_critique: Demo paper with one use case; highlights, rather than solves, the energy cost of AI-native network control.

title: Study on energy efficiency and energy saving aspects of 5G networks and services
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA5 Rel-19 study on new energy-consumption, EE and energy-saving KPIs and management use cases, including VNF/VNFC energy estimation, energy-information exposure, slice energy metrics and renewable-energy-aware optimisation.
method: standard (management study)
key_result: Recommends normative extensions to TS 28.310 and related management specifications for energy information and saving.
limitation_or_critique: Management-plane study; leaves the analytics and optimisation methods for core energy saving to vendors and research.

title: Energy-Aware VNF-FG Placement with Transformer-based Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Rania Sahraoui; Omar Houidi; Fetia Bannour
venue: NOMS 2024-2024 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Proposes TDRL, an actor-critic DRL agent with a GAT encoder for the substrate and a Transformer seq2seq encoder for VNF forwarding graphs, for online energy-aware placement.
method: DRL with graph attention + Transformer
key_result: Learns placements that improve acceptance and reduce energy compared with baseline DRL and heuristics in large dynamic settings.
limitation_or_critique: Generic VNF-FG model, not 5GC-specific; simulation-only with an abstract server power model.

title: VNF Placement and Dynamic NUMA Node Selection Through Core Consolidation at the Edge and Cloud
authors: Taha Ben Salah; Marios Avgeris; Aris Leivadeas; Ioannis Lambadaris
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Formulates SFC placement across edge and cloud as a MIP that also chooses NUMA nodes and CPU cores, and proposes the DySCo consolidation heuristic.
method: MIP + heuristic (DySCo)
key_result: Shows that consolidating at core and NUMA granularity, not only server level, improves resource and energy efficiency for delay-sensitive SFCs.
limitation_or_critique: Not specific to 5GC NFs; no learning component and no hardware power validation.

title: HADES: An NFV solution for energy-efficient placement and resource allocation in heterogeneous infrastructures
authors: Angel Cañete; Mercedes Amor; Lidia Fuentes
venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications
summary: Extends ETSI Open Source MANO with an energy-aware SFC placement and resource-allocation module for heterogeneous IoT/edge/cloud hosts.
method: heuristic placement integrated in OSM
data_or_testbed: real and simulated AR service deployments
key_result: Reports up to 59% lower power than default OSM placement and four other policies with negligible overhead.
limitation_or_critique: Use case is an AR service chain rather than a 5G core; heuristic, not learning-based.

title: Study on Energy Efficiency as service criteria
authors: 3GPP
summary: SA1 Rel-19 stage-1 study defining use cases where energy consumption and efficiency become service criteria, e.g. energy information for users and energy-limited service delivery.
method: standard (service requirements study)
key_result: Leads to the EnergyServ service requirements in TS 22.261 that drive the SA2 and SA5 energy work.
limitation_or_critique: Stage-1 requirements only; no architecture, metrics or algorithms.

title: Zero-Touch AI-Driven Distributed Management for Energy-Efficient 6G Massive Network Slicing
authors: Hatim Chergui; Luis Blanco; Luis A. Garrido; Kostas Ramantas; Slawomir Kuklinski; Adlen Ksentini; Christos Verikoukis
summary: Discusses architectural and AI design options for energy efficiency in 6G and proposes a statistical federated-learning analytic engine for slice-level resource prediction under SLA constraints.
method: statistical federated learning (proxy-Lagrangian)
key_result: Shows that SLA-constrained federated prediction enables energy-efficient zero-touch slice resource provisioning.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style article; energy savings are indirect and the RAN/core resources are modelled abstractly.
